items.title: Burkina Faso : Le Premier ministre lance la récolte du maïs à l’aide de moissonneuses-batteuses
items.description: Le Premier ministre, Rimtalba Jean-Emmanuel Ouédraogo, accompagné du commandant Ismaël Sombié, ministre d'État chargé de l'Agriculture, et de quelques membres du gouvernement, a effectué, ce 20 octobre 2026, une visite de terrain dans la province du Boulgou, région du Nakambé. À cette occasion, il a lancé la récolte du maïs à Bagré, procédé à l'inauguration de la rizerie de SOFA et lancé officiellement l'opération d'aménagement commando de 50 000 hectares de périmètres irrigués dans la commune de Niaogho. Avant ces étapes, le chef du gouvernement est allé constater le déroulement de la campagne de vaccination contre les maladies animales à Rimvoussé, dans la commune de Zonsé. Sur place, il a noté les innovations apportées à cette campagne, notamment l'introduction du bolus pour l'identification du cheptel, la baisse des coûts ainsi que la gratuité de certains vaccins au profit des éleveurs. la campagne de vaccination contre les maladies animales©️Faso7 À cet effet, il a souligné l'importance de ce secteur dans l'Offensive agropastorale et halieutique. Selon ses explications, il est prévu la production d’au moins 100 000 tonnes de poisson pour couvrir 65 % de la consommation nationale. En ce qui concerne la production laitière et ses dérivés, ce sont 75 millions de litres de lait transformé qui sont attendus pour satisfaire 50 % des besoins. Ce plan prévoit aussi l'exportation de près de 35 000 tonnes de viande par an. Pour y parvenir, il a rappelé la construction d’abattoirs modernes dans plusieurs villes afin de générer de la richesse nationale. « C'était la première halte de supervision, et il faut dire que nous sommes pleinement satisfaits de ce que nous avons vu, non seulement en termes d'organisation générale de cette campagne, mais aussi d'adhésion de la population. Je pense que les premières données et les premières statistiques montrent que, évidemment, ce sont des objectifs certes ambitieux, mais si les choses se poursuivent ainsi, nous devons pouvoir les atteindre », a-t-il signifié. Ces machines permettent de récolter et d’égrener le maïs afin de rendre les grains rapidement disponibles Après cette étape, le Premier ministre, avec à ses côtés le ministre chargé de l’Agriculture, a lancé la récolte du maïs à l’aide de moissonneuses-batteuses. Ces machines permettent de récolter et d’égrener simultanément le maïs afin de rendre les grains rapidement disponibles. Avec une capacité de traitement de 10 hectares par jour, elles peuvent fonctionner entre 8 et 10 heures quotidiennement. Le Premier ministre a rappelé que la mécanisation de l'agriculture constitue une condition sine qua non pour l'atteinte de la souveraineté alimentaire. À cet égard, chaque commune du Burkina Faso a été dotée d'une brigade de mécanisation qui a contribué à l'obtention de bonnes récoltes. Il a ainsi souligné que l’octroi des moissonneuses-batteuses intervient pour parfaire le processus de récolte. « C'est ça aussi la vision de la Révolution progressiste populaire, qui est que, dans le cadre de cette offensive agropastorale et halieutique, mais aussi hydraulique pour cette phase 2, c'est évidemment de poursuivre la modernisation de l'agriculture, d'accompagner nos producteurs pour réduire la pénibilité tout en augmentant les rendements, mais aussi la productivité », a-t-il ajouté. La rizerie de SOFA©️Faso7 Par ailleurs, le Premier ministre a inauguré, dans la commune de Bagré, la Rizerie de la Société Faso Agropoles (SOFA). Cette unité industrielle dispose d'une capacité de transformation de 100 tonnes de riz par jour. Elle a été bâtie afin de faciliter la transformation du surplus de production rizicole. En 2025, le Burkina Faso a atteint un million de tonnes de riz paddy produit. Cela s'est fait grâce à l'Offensive agropastorale et halieutique ainsi qu'à l'Initiative présidentielle pour la production agricole et l'autosuffisance alimentaire. Au lancement de l'opération d'aménagement commando de 50 000 hectares de périmètres irrigués, le Premier ministre a indiqué que cette initiative comporte deux volets. Le volet « Urgence » concerne l'augmentation de la disponibilité en eau, d'où le lancement du programme de forages à prix subventionné. Au niveau structurel, il s'agit de l'aménagement de 50 000 hectares supplémentaires de périmètres irrigués. Il a rappelé qu'avant cette opération, le pays ne comptait que 30 000 hectares irrigués. D'un coût de réalisation estimé à 250 milliards de F CFA, ces nouvelles superficies devraient permettre d'effectuer trois cycles de production par an. « Au terme de cette opération commando, le visage du secteur agricole burkinabè ne sera plus le même. Il va être complètement transformé, parce que nous allons passer aujourd'hui d'à peu près 30 000 hectares de superficies irriguées à plus de 80 000 hectares de superficies irriguées. C'est un moment historique que nous sommes en train de vivre, et nous sommes convaincus que nous allons y arriver, parce que, évidemment, la révolution progressiste et populaire ne compose pas avec l'échec ; nous ne composons qu'avec la réussite et la victoire » , a-t-il déclaré. Cheick Habib Désiré BAYILI Faso7 L’article Burkina Faso : Le Premier ministre lance la récolte du maïs à l’aide de moissonneuses-batteuses est apparu en premier sur Faso7 .

items.title: Champions League: Foden hat-trick help Man City rout AEK Athens
items.description: Phil Foden hit a hat-trick to underline his long-awaited return to form as Manchester City crushed AEK Athens 5-1 in the Champions League on Tuesday. After a significant dip over the last two seasons, Foden provided hope of a renaissance for the England playmaker with a sublime display at the Etihad Stadium. The 26-year-old, who has admitted struggling with mental health issues, hadn’t scored for 10 months prior to his goal in Saturday’s win against Ipswich. Long heralded as one of England’s brightest talents, Foden was left out of his country’s World Cup squad earlier this year in a damning sign of his fall from grace. Having ended his run without a goal in the Champions League since November 2025, Foden now has to produce nights like this on a regular basis to complete his revival. Elliot Anderson put City ahead early in the first half with his first goal for the club since his close-season move from Nottingham Forest. Foden doubled City’s lead before the break and although Stavros Pilios pulled one back for the Greek side after the interval, the Premier League leaders finished with a flourish. Rayan Cherki bagged City’s third goal in typically flamboyant fashion and Foden struck twice more to complete his treble. It was City’s second win in the league phase after beating Porto in their opening game and losing to holders Paris Saint-Germain last week. City’s future remains in limbo as they wait the result of their appeal against an independent commission’s verdict that they were guilty of more than 100 breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules. With reports emerging that City are set to be hit with a massive points deduction that will almost certainly condemn them to relegation, this season’s Champions League campaign could be the club’s last for some time. Enzo Maresca and his players have shown little sign of being affected by the scandal, while City’s fans defiantly show their backing for the Abu Dhabi-owned club. They have won 10 of their 11 games in all competitions this season and even the absence of Erling Haaland couldn’t derail them. Manchester City’s English midfielder #47 Phil Foden celebrates scoring the team’s fourth goal during the UEFA Champions League football match between Manchester City and AEK Athens at the Etihad Stadium in Manchester, north west England, on October 20, 2026. (Photo by Oli SCARFF / AFP) – Fantastic Foden – City started with Haaland on the bench after the Norway striker limped down the tunnel at the final whistle with a foot injury following his double against Ipswich. Maresca made eight changes from the Ipswich game, with 17-year-old academy graduate Floyd Samba showing flashes of his talent on the flanks. City’s understudies took just 12 minutes to seize the lead. Enzo Fernadez’s free-kick cannoned down off the bar and Anderson reacted quicker than the flat-footed AEK defence as the midfielder slotted into the empty net from 10 yards. Foden doubled City’s lead at the climax of an eye-catching move in the 34th minute. Exchanging passes in a blur of movement and precision, Foden and Rico Lewis cut through AEK with ease before Foden fired high into the roof of the net from an acute angle. Perhaps overconfident after such a one-sided half, City lost their focus, allowing Pilios to reduce the deficit with their first shot on target in the 52nd minute. City quickly regained their two-goal lead in the 57th minute. Picked out by Foden on the edge of the area, Cherki unfurled a balletic turn that took him into space for a fine finish in keeping with his graceful first touch. In the 65th minute, Cherki’s long ball was knocked down by Lewis and Foden arrived to caress his shot into the top corner from 18 yards. Foden made a perfectly-timed run to tap home Ryan McAidoo’s cross in the 76th minute, sealing his first hat-trick for over two years. items.title: BBC Three, BBC Scotland and Radio 4 Extra broadcast channels to close
items.description: The BBC will close its BBC Three and BBC Scotland television channels in the spring, as the corporation continues to save £500m over two years. Both services will become online-only, meaning they will continue to produce and host some content on iPlayer, without the need to fill a terrestrial TV schedule. The BBC has also announced the closure of Radio 4 Extra, which largely airs speech programmes from the BBC’s archive, including comedy, drama and documentaries. BBC director-general Matt Brittin said: “We need to make every pound work harder for audiences as we respond to the immediate cost pressures and reinvent the BBC for a changing world. We all know that means tough choices.” Discussing the closure of linear broadcast services, Brittin said: “Much of the great content they currently carry will still be found where audiences already enjoy them on iPlayer and Sounds. “While this follows media speculation, I recognise the confirmation of this news will be hard for audiences and colleagues.” Outlining the plans, the corporation confirmed: BBC Scotland will remain a channel on iPlayer , with some content also broadcast on BBC One and BBC Two in Scotland BBC Three commissions, supported by increased investment in content for younger audiences, will be available on BBC iPlayer and on other platforms including YouTube Some programmes that air on Radio 4 Extra will be available on BBC Sounds – while its religious programme The Daily Service will be on BBC Sounds and local radio BBC Three launched hits including Gavin & Stacey, which returned for a Christmas finale in 2024 BBC Three, aimed at young audiences and home to hits such as Fleabag, Normal People and Gavin & Stacey, moved online in 2016 but was reinstated as a TV channel in 2022. BBC Scotland launched as a channel in 2019, broadcasting a variety of Scottish programming including news, sport, documentaries and entertainment. However, some shows on the two networks, such as Two Doors Down on BBC Scotland and Sort Your Life Out on BBC Three, are repeats of episodes originally broadcast on other, more mainstream BBC channels. Both networks currently broadcast TV programming only in the evenings, although BBC Scotland simulcasts BBC Radio Scotland for the rest of the day. The BBC said that the network’s nightly programme Reporting Scotland: News at Seven will not move to BBC iPlayer and will cease when the linear channel closes. BBC Scotland’s wider news offering will continue to serve audiences, including Reporting Scotland, The Sunday Show, Radio Scotland Breakfast, Debate Night and Scotcast, the corporation said. While Radio 4 Extra airs some original programming, its schedule is mostly archive content, much of which is available on BBC Sounds. Sir Peter Bazalgette, former chairman of ITV and production company Endemol, told BBC News: “This is a modest and pretty well-judged package. “The essence of it is it protects the spending on content, it really cuts money in the distribution of programmes, and it really had to happen because the BBC has lost 30% of its revenue in 10 years.” But entertainment trade union Equity said Tuesday’s announcement “does not signal a thriving BBC, and we are concerned about the UK’s preeminent public service broadcaster’s ability to meet its duties to the fullest”. Staff affected by the changes were told on Tuesday, although some media outlets had reported the proposed closure of BBC Scotland and BBC Three in recent weeks. The BBC aims to cut between 1,800 and 2,000 jobs, almost one in 10, to save £500m over two years as it faces “significant financial pressures”. Around 550 job closures have already been announced in the news, while BBC Sport has so far announced more than 30 job cuts. The newly appointed director of BBC News, Rachel Jupp, announced on Tuesday that the BBC is proposing a further £5.5m in savings, which would mean closing around 100 roles. Meanwhile, the BBC has cancelled several high-profile TV series in recent weeks.The BBC has dropped RuPaul’s Drag Race UK, Blankety Blank, Celebrity Mastermind, Live at the Apollo, Football Focus, Ski Sunday, and Radio 4’s The World Tonight and You & Yours so far.

items.title: Elon Musk says Tesla-SpaceX merger being considered
items.description: Elon Musk said he likes the idea of merging Tesla and SpaceX, two of his most notable companies, and that it is under active consideration. “Do I think it would be a good idea? Yes,” Musk said during a call with financial analysts over the quarterly business results of SpaceX on Tuesday. While Musk noted that such a merger is not certain and would need shareholders’ support, he said special committees within both companies have been formed to examine the move. “The special committees have not reached agreement on terms of any transaction, and there’s no guarantee that they will,” Musk added. “But I do think there is a lot of merit to merging and a lot to be gained.” With Tesla valued at roughly $1.5 trillion and SpaceX at $2 trillion, combining the two companies would mark one of the largest mergers in history. Over the last year, Musk has brought more of his companies under fewer banners. Before it went public earlier this year, SpaceX acquired xAI and X, the platform formerly known as Twitter, both of which Musk owned. The recent launch of Terafab, a joint effort between Tesla and SpaceX to manufacture computer chips, was another signal that Musk sees his companies as potentially more effective when working together. Musk said on Tuesday that a full merger between the two companies would make sense given the work each is doing on chips, artificial intelligence, software, and more. Musk, who became the world’s first paper trillionaire after SpaceX’s stock market debut earlier this year, said he is not on either of the special committees considering the mega-merger. He described himself as a “conflicted party” as Tesla and SpaceX’s chief executive. Even commenting on a possible merger between the two companies, Musk compared it to “tap dancing through a minefield”. He added that shareholders would ultimately decide on a merger. At least 50% of Tesla’s shareholders would need to approve the merger, which Musk described as “quite a high hurdle to achieve”. Shareholders have supported Musk’s desires before. Last year, a majority of Tesla investors approved a compensation package for Musk valued at around $1 trillion. While Tesla is known as an electric car company, Musk has recently shifted resources to focus on robotics. SpaceX quickly outstripped Tesla in market value when it made its stock market debut. The company, which builds space rockets and Starlink internet satellites, is now expanding into offering cloud compute capacity for other tech companies, like Anthropic and Google. That line of business is now SpaceX’s most profitable, bringing in $7.5bn, according to the latest quarterly results.

items.title: Ligue des champions : Manchester City corrige l’AEK Athènes
items.description: Manchester City a largement dominé l’AEK Athènes (5-1), mardi soir, à l’Etihad Stadium, lors de la troisième journée de la phase de ligue de la Ligue des champions. Portés par un Phil Foden étincelant, auteur d’un triplé, les Anglais se relancent après leur défaite contre le Paris Saint-Germain. Manchester City a retrouvé le sourire sur la scène européenne. Battus par le PSG (2-4) lors de la précédente journée, les hommes d’Enzo Maresca ont réagi avec autorité en s’imposant 5-1 face à l’AEK Athènes, mardi 20 octobre, devant leur public. Les Citizens ont rapidement pris les commandes de la rencontre grâce à Elliot Anderson, buteur à la 12e minute. Phil Foden a ensuite doublé la mise à la 34e minute, permettant aux Anglais de rejoindre les vestiaires avec deux buts d’avance. Au retour des vestiaires, les Grecs ont tenté de relancer le suspense. Stavros Pilios a réduit l’écart à la 52e minute, mais la réaction de Manchester City ne s’est pas fait attendre. Rayan Cherki a inscrit le troisième but des locaux à la 57e minute, redonnant de l’air à son équipe. Foden a ensuite pris les choses en main. Le milieu offensif anglais a inscrit deux nouveaux buts aux 65e et 76e minutes, complétant ainsi son triplé et scellant le large succès de son équipe. Cette performance individuelle confirme le rôle important de Foden dans l’animation offensive mancunienne. Manchester City a également démontré la profondeur de son effectif, malgré les absences offensives enregistrées avant cette rencontre. Avec cette victoire, le club anglais se relance dans la course à la qualification pour la suite de la Ligue des champions. L’AEK Athènes, de son côté, devra rapidement réagir après cette lourde défaite européenne.

Burkina/Justice : La peine de mort réintroduite dans le Code pénal, des sanctions revues à la hausse
items.description: Le ministre de la Justice et des droits humains, Me Edasso Rodrigue Bayala, a défendu, ce mardi 20 octobre 2026 devant les parlementaires de l'Assemblée législative du peuple (ALP), le projet de loi portant relecture de la loi n°025-2018/AN du 25 mai 2018 portant Code pénal au Burkina Faso. Au terme des votes, l'ALP a adopté à l'unanimité de ses 71 parlementaires, la nouvelle loi portant Code pénal au Burkina Faso, avec la réintroduction de la peine de mort (qui avait été abolie le 31 mai 2018) . Cette réforme législative vise à, selon le ministre de la Justice et des droits humains, renforcer l'ordre public, à consolider les valeurs fondamentales de la Nation et à garantir la sécurité des personnes et des biens. Elle permet d'introduire des innovations majeures visant à adapter le dispositif pénal aux exigences de protection de la société et de lutte contre les différentes formes de criminalité. ‎ Parlant des orientations générales du Code pénal qui vient d'être adopté, Me Edasso Rodrigue Bayala explique qu'il vise d'abord à contribuer à la lutte contre le terrorisme au Burkina Faso. Ensuite, contribuer à protéger suffisamment l'ordre public, lutter contre la criminalité économique et financière au Burkina, protéger l'environnement, la famille et également à assurer l'ordre public au niveau de la sécurité routière. Comme innovations majeures, le premier responsable du département de la Justice et des droits humains, Me Bayala, énumère la restauration de la peine pour un certain nombre d'infractions qui sont en lien avec le terrorisme. Sur ce point, le ministre fait le constat que sur le terrain, les terroristes recrutent en faisant comprendre également aux candidats qu'ils ne risquent pas gros en matière de peines, même s'ils venaient à être arrêtés, et comme auteurs ou complices. Aussi, poursuit-il, l'espionnage et la trahison sont désormais passibles de la peine de mort, tout comme l'importation de produits périmés ou prohibés, lorsque cela entraîne la mort (et ce, aussi bien pour l'auteur que pour le complice de l'acte). Lire aussi : Burkina/Justice : La peine de mort rétablie et les peines d'amende relevées La criminalité économique et financière est dorénavant punie d'un emprisonnement à vie, à partir d'un certain montant pour le détournement, et d'une peine d'amende correspondant au triple du montant détourné. Le Code pénal qui vient d'être adopté se caractérise aussi par le durcissement des peines en matière de sécurité routière (les statistiques montrant que l'insécurité routière est la première cause de mortalité au Burkina). Des comportements en circulation qui n'étaient pas appréhendés le sont maintenant et punis par des peines d'emprisonnement. Plusieurs autres peines sont revues à la hausse, en faisant passer des infractions de contravention à délit (donc punies de peine d'emprisonnement). Au niveau de la famille, le Code réaffirme la pénalisation de l'homosexualité et pratiques assimilées. Pour ce qui est de la protection de l'environnement, les peines d'amende ont également été revues à la hausse, pour permettre une sanction suffisante et décourager d'éventuels candidats. Le phénomène d'abattage et d'exportation des ânes et chevaux est repris dans le Code pénal et sanctionné. Par ailleurs, le Code intègre des infractions nouvelles liées aux technologies de l'information et de la communication. Au terme des votes, l'ALP a adopté à l'unanimité de ses 71 parlementaires, la nouvelle loi portant Code pénal au Burkina Faso Lire aussi : Situation nationale : « Burkina Remparts » pour un retour à la peine de mort et la saisie des biens des personnes en accointance avec l'ennemi O.L. items.title: Main suspect accused of visa fraud in student's suicide case killed in firing by accomplices: police
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The prime suspect accused of defrauding a 20-year-old student, who died allegedly by suicide, was killed after being shot by his accomplices in Islamabad on Tuesday, claimed police. Laiba Ijaz, a student at International Islamic University, was said to have been defrauded of Rs5 million, which she had paid to move to the United States for further studies. An agent was accused of handing her fake travel documents. The case drew the government’s attention, with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif directing the police to arrest the suspect. Subsequently, he and two of his female accomplices were picked up during separate raids in the federal capital. According to the Islamabad police spokesperson, the prime suspect sustained injuries when his accomplices opened fire on cops in the jurisdiction of Ramna police station on Tuesday. The spokesperson said the main suspect has shared information about another suspect, and a police team was taking him to track down the second suspect. It was then that four of the main suspect’s accomplices, who were on two motorcycles, “opened indiscriminate fire on the police party in an attempt get the main suspect freed”, the spokesperson added. The main suspect was injured in the firing while the police team remained safe “due to bulletproof jackets and protective measures”, the spokesperson said. The injured suspect was taken to a hospital, where he succumbed to his injuries, he added. Search operations were underway for arrest of his other accomplices, the spokesperson said. The case A case following Ijaz’s death was registered at the Ramna police station under Sections 322 (unintentional murder) and 34 (acts done by several persons in furtherance of common intention) of the Pakistan Penal Code. Another separate case was registered by the Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) on a complaint filed by Ijaz’s maternal uncle under provisions relating to cheating, abetment and immigration-related fraud. According to the FIA, the main suspect had allegedly obtained millions of rupees from Ijaz’s family with the help of a female accomplice and by misrepresenting his identity and professional status. The money was allegedly taken on the pretext of securing employment for her brother and arranging her admission to Harvard University in the US. The suspect was accused of giving Ijaz fake travel documents.

items.title: Turkish FA bans 147 officials for breaching betting rules
items.description: Trabzonspor president Ertugrul Dogan has been named among 147 football club officials to receive 45-day bans from the Turkish Football Federation (TFF) for breaching betting rules. In September, the TFF announced that it had provisionally suspended 448 people and referred them to its professional football disciplinary board over allegations they placed bets while in office. Like players and coaches, TFF regulations, along with those of FIFA and UEFA, forbid match officials from participating in betting activities. The TFF said the people involved had held posts at clubs in the top two divisions in Turkish football over the previous five years. Of those, some 147 breached betting rules and will be barred from carrying out duties in football during the suspension period. There were insufficient grounds for disciplinary action in the other 301 cases. The Turkish football authorities have clamped down on betting in the sport over the last year. In November 2025, a TFF investigation handed bans to 149 referees and 1,204 players.

items.title: FGMSA sues Medical and Dental Council to halt Common Registration Examination
items.description: The Federation of Ghana Medical Students’ Associations (FGMSA) and affected graduating medical and dental students have sued the Medical and Dental Council (MDC), seeking to restrain the regulator from conducting the Common Registration Examination (CRE). In a statement issued on Tuesday, October 20, 2026, and signed by its National Executive Council, FGMSA said the case had been filed at the High Court’s Human Rights Division in Accra. The applicants are seeking an injunction to prevent the examination from being conducted pending the determination of the substantive legal issues before the court. The action follows unsuccessful attempts to resolve their concerns through engagement with the relevant authorities, according to the Federation. “FGMSA remains committed to protecting the interests of medical and dental students and will pursue the legal process to its conclusion,” the statement said. The Common Registration Examination is a new licensing examination introduced by the MDC for graduating medical and dental students. Its implementation has drawn opposition from some students, who have raised concerns about the examination and its potential implications for their careers. FGMSA said it had previously engaged the MDC and other relevant authorities in an effort to resolve the concerns, but those efforts did not produce an agreement, prompting the legal action. The application seeks to prevent the MDC from proceeding with the examination while the court considers the issues raised by the applicants. The specific legal arguments and reliefs sought beyond the injunction were not detailed in the statement. The timing of the hearing and whether the court will grant the injunction were also not specified. The case is therefore pending, and the court’s decision will determine whether the examination can proceed while the substantive legal challenge remains before it. FGMSA-CRE-Legal-statement Download

items.title: Audit regulator looking into Manchester City accounting
items.description: The UK audit regulator has confirmed it is leading inquiries into accounting irregularities at Manchester City. The Financial Reporting Council confirmed in a letter to the House of Commons Business, Culture, and Sport Committee that it had taken over “regulatory consideration” of the case from the Institute of Chartered Accountants in England and Wales on 30 September. No formal investigation has started, but the FRC is investigating the case. This follows an independent commission finding Manchester City guilty of all charges relating to breaches of the Premier League’s financial regulations between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 seasons, including artificially inflating the club’s financial position by more than £900m. City are appealing the verdict. The FRC has greater resources and powers to impose sanctions if it finds evidence of violations. It routinely oversees accounting standards at bigger institutions such as listed public companies, but not football clubs. The FRC can investigate the conduct of BDO, Manchester City’s auditors, to determine whether the audit complied with the rules. It can also sanction individuals, such as directors or employees of the Etihad club, if they are members of professional accountancy bodies. BDO is the UK’s fifth-biggest accounting firm, but claims to be a market leader in football, advising more Premier League and Championship clubs than any other firm. The independent commission that investigated Manchester City found that the club gave its auditors a “misleading impression” of the scheme used to disguise the origin of shareholder funds injected into the club, and that the auditors were “unaware” of the scheme. Manchester City said it will appeal the commission’s decision, arguing it contains “material errors of law, principle and fact and is unsafe”. Liam Byrne, chair of the business select committee, called for greater powers for the FRC to look into similar cases. He wrote on X: “The regulator’s letter exposes gaps in its ability to compel evidence from the club and pursue directors who fall outside its disciplinary rules. “This raises serious questions about the powers available to hold companies and directors to account. “The government has a responsibility to explain why reforms to close these gaps were abandoned – and what will now be done to strengthen accountability.” BDO declined to comment.

items.title: Doue impresses as PSG beat Barcelona in thriller
items.description: Desire Doue, Lamine Yamal and Vitinha scored superb individual goals as Champions League holders Paris St-Germain overcame Barcelona in a breathless encounter at Parc des Princes. After starring in PSG’s victory against Manchester City last week, Doue opened the scoring in the 38th minute of a first half in which both sides missed several clear chances. Teenage full-back Xavi Espart drew Barcelona level early in the second half with a rifled near-post effort, before PSG defender Lucas Hernandez powered in a towering header. Lamine Yamal made it 2-2 with a genius near-post finish, but less than two minutes later Vitinha sent a volley into the bottom corner to reclaim the lead for PSG. Fabian Ruiz put the result beyond doubt five minutes later by converting Achraf Hakimi’s low cross at the back post, in a win that ends Barcelona’s 11-match unbeaten run at the start of their season. The Parisians had wasted little time in implementing their high-pressing gameplan to force Barcelona into several mistakes in the early stages. The game was 79 seconds old when Khvicha Kvaratskhelia struck the foot of the post after Pedri was dispossessed, before Doue and Ousmane Dembele were denied by Barca goalkeeper Joan Garcia following high turnovers. It was then Barcelona’s turn to launch their own rapid attacks, but Raphinha could only fire straight at Matvey Safonov in the PSG goal after running on to a neat Anthony Gordon pass. Garcia had a busy end to the half as he twice denied former Barcelona team-mate Ferran Torres – who replaced the injured Dembele – but the goalkeeper could do nothing about Doue’s opener. After PSG intercepted a Barca ball out from defence, Doue drove to the edge of the penalty area and rifled a low shot into the bottom left corner. Minutes before half-time Fermin Lopez was thwarted in a one-on-one situation by Safonov, but 10 minutes into the second half Espart, 19, beat the Russian goalkeeper at his near post after bursting into the box. Barcelona were starting to look the more likely side to claim a winner, but, moments after Torres hit the post following a quick counter, Hernandez planted a header past Garcia from a corner. Out of nothing, Lamine Yamal then turned Warren Zaire-Emery, sprinted into the box and squeezed the ball in between Safonov and the post. Just as the momentum looked to have swung in Barca’s favour, Vitinha controlled a clearance with his chest before launching a stunning volley into the bottom corner, before Ruiz put the seal on an exhilarating match. PSG have nine points and will next face Villarreal in Spain on Tuesday, 3 November (20:00 GMT). Barcelona remain on six points and will host Aston Villa at Camp Nou at the same time.

items.title: Loi de finances rectificative : Amadou Ba appelle à un compromis pour éviter l’impasse
items.description: Dans un texte intitulé « Appel à la responsabilité nationale », le député et ancien Premier ministre Amadou Ba met en garde contre un risque d'impasse budgétaire. Les divergences autour de l'adoption de la loi de finances rectificative (LFR) 2026, et leurs prolongements possibles sur le prochain exercice, pourraient, selon lui, fragiliser la stabilité institutionnelle et économique du pays. Il demande au chef de l'État, au gouvernement et à l'Assemblée nationale d'engager sans délai une concertation. Un risque d'impasse qui ne doit pas se muer en paralysie Pour l'élu, le Sénégal aborde « une séquence particulièrement délicate » de son histoire économique et institutionnelle. Il rappelle que le désaccord est consubstantiel à la démocratie, mais qu'il ne doit jamais se transformer en paralysie de l'État. Le moment est d'autant plus sensible, souligne-t-il, que le pays mène des discussions décisives avec le Fonds monétaire international (FMI) et ses créanciers. Il faut donc préserver la cohérence des choix budgétaires, la confiance des partenaires et la stabilité de l'économie. Amadou Ba insiste sur l'enjeu immédiat. Sans adoption de la LFR, près de 540 milliards de FCFA de subventions énergétiques risqueraient de rester sans crédits budgétaires suffisants. Il y voit non pas une économie pour l'État, mais un risque d'impayés, d'accumulation d'arriérés et, à terme, d'alourdissement du coût de la dette. Il estime qu'un compromis doit être trouvé avant la fin de l'exercice budgétaire. Les préoccupations liées au pouvoir d'achat, aux dépenses sociales, à l'investissement et aux subventions énergétiques sont légitimes, reconnaît-il. Mais la discipline budgétaire et la justice sociale ne sauraient être opposées. La responsabilité de gouverner, écrit-il, consiste précisément à les concilier. Il en appelle « solennellement » au Président de la République, au gouvernement et à la représentation nationale pour qu'ils engagent une concertation institutionnelle, afin de dégager un compromis sur les orientations budgétaires essentielles. Cette démarche devrait se faire dans le respect des prérogatives de chaque institution, de l'État de droit et de l'autorité des décisions de justice. Des Assises de l'économie, une idée remise sur la table Amadou Ba rappelle avoir préconisé, lors du dialogue national, la tenue d'Assises sur l'économie, convaincu que les défis structurels du pays appelaient un diagnostic partagé. Les circonstances actuelles, estime-t-il, confortent cette proposition. Fort de son expérience de Premier ministre et de ministre des Finances, il affirme qu'en matière économique, l'incertitude a un coût, l'inaction en a un autre, et que ce sont toujours les populations qui en paient le prix. Aucune divergence politique, conclut-il, ne justifie d'exposer à des risques évitables la stabilité des institutions, la crédibilité financière de l'État et les conditions de vie des citoyens. « L'heure n'est pas à l'épreuve de force, mais à l'épreuve de responsabilité », écrit-il, ajoutant que l'intérêt supérieur de la Nation « commande le dialogue, exige le compromis et oblige chacun ».

items.title: Énergie, eau, semences : la souveraineté érigée en doctrine
items.description: Stocks stratégiques, 18 GW supplémentaires, près de 400 barrages, autonomie semencière, Cloud souverain : le programme gouvernemental donne à la souveraineté un contenu bien plus large que la protection du territoire, en l’adossant à la maîtrise des ressources dont dépend la résilience du pays. Dans un environnement mondial instable, aggravé par des pressions climatiques récurrentes, le programme gouvernemental consacre une conception élargie de la souveraineté. Celle-ci ne se réduit plus à la défense des frontières : elle s’étend à la maîtrise des ressources stratégiques indispensables à la résilience nationale. Six piliers structurent cette vision : la sécurité énergétique, la gestion durable de l’eau, l’autonomie alimentaire, la montée en gamme industrielle, l’innovation technologique et le renforcement des capacités de défense. L’Exécutif entend ainsi prémunir le pays contre les chocs extérieurs, sans repli autarcique, tout en consolidant son rôle de hub industriel et énergétique régional. Le volet énergétique conjugue sécurisation à court terme et déploiement massif des renouvelables. Le Programme instaure l’obligation de maintenir un stock national de sécurité en hydrocarbures couvrant au moins trois mois de consommation. Il prévoit parallèlement d’injecter près de 18 gigawatts de capacités électriques dans le réseau, à travers de grands complexes solaires et éoliens : Midelt 1, 2 et 3 (990 MW), Tahaddart 2 et 3 (1 400 MW), Nador (1 200 MW) et le programme éolien En-Nassim (1 120 MW). Ces capacités seront accompagnées d’environ 2 230 MW de batteries de stockage et de stations de transfert d’énergie par pompage (STEP), pour améliorer le rendement des réseaux. L’objectif est de porter la part des énergies renouvelables à 52 % du mix électrique d’ici 2030. Un taux d’intégration locale d’au moins 50 % sera imposé à l’horizon 2031 dans l’ensemble des projets du secteur, et deux zones industrielles dédiées à la fabrication d’équipements verts doivent réduire le coût d’accès à l’électricité propre pour les PME. La stratégie englobe également la réalisation d’infrastructures de gaz naturel liquéfié (réception, stockage, regazéification), le suivi du tracé du gazoduc Nigéria-Maroc et l’accompagnement des investisseurs dans l’hydrogène vert et l’ammoniac. Face au stress hydrique structurel, la politique de l’eau change d’échelle en misant sur les ressources non conventionnelles. Six nouvelles stations de dessalement d’eau de mer doivent permettre de dépasser 1,8 milliard de mètres cubes par an d’ici 2031. Le Programme prévoit aussi la finalisation du second tronçon d’interconnexion entre les bassins de l’Oum Er-Rbia, de Lalla Takerkoust, du Bouregreg et du Sebou, afin de rééquilibrer le potentiel hydrique national, ainsi que la réalisation de près de 400 barrages et retenues d’eaux pluviales. Du côté de la demande, l’irrigation goutte-à-goutte sera étendue à 350 000 hectares supplémentaires, pour atteindre 1,2 million d’hectares équipés, soit près de 70 % des surfaces irriguées. Le recyclage des eaux usées traitées sera accéléré pour l’arrosage des espaces verts et des golfs, comme pour l’usage industriel. Dans le monde rural, plus de 1 000 points d’eau seront aménagés et le pastoralisme développé afin de préserver le cheptel. La souveraineté alimentaire repose sur la protection des capacités de production et la réduction de la dépendance aux intrants étrangers. Un programme national d’autonomie semencière doit faire passer la part des semences nationales de 20 à 50 %, avec l’appui de banques de gènes locales chargées de préserver la diversité variétale. Le semis direct sera adopté sur un million d’hectares à l’horizon 2030 pour renforcer la résistance des céréales à la sécheresse, et les programmes d’assurance contre les aléas climatiques extrêmes seront élargis. L’approvisionnement en engrais phosphatés sera, lui, régulé, en coordination avec le Groupe OCP, pour garantir des prix stables aux agriculteurs. Pour la filière animale, la stratégie associe numérisation et traçabilité électronique du cheptel, via le Système national d’identification et de traçabilité, et soutien direct aux petits et moyens éleveurs afin de préserver la reproduction des races locales, comme le Sardi, le Timahdite et le D’man. Elle vise une couverture sanitaire d’au moins 85 % des animaux. La société BIOPHARMA sera modernisée selon les standards de l’industrie 4.0, afin de produire localement les vaccins vétérinaires critiques et les kits de diagnostic. L’indépendance économique s’appuie par ailleurs sur une intégration industrielle plus stricte. La Charte de l’Investissement conditionne désormais les subventions de l’État au taux d’intégration locale effectif, à la création d’emplois qualifiés et au volume de R&D réalisé sur place, avec des cibles de 80 % dans l’automobile et de 60 % dans l’aéronautique à l’horizon 2031. Cette dynamique inclut la relocalisation de la fabrication de composants critiques : composants électroniques, batteries LFP (lithium-fer-phosphate), logiciels embarqués, câblage avancé, chimie fine et équipements électriques. L'Exécutif s’engage aussi à structurer un pôle industriel de défense et de sécurité compétitif, fédérant recherche, ingénierie, fabrication d’équipements et maintenance. Il s’appuiera sur des partenariats internationaux, notamment des joint-ventures avec des acteurs de premier plan, assortis de clauses de transfert de technologie effectifs. Sur le plan numérique, le gouvernement déploie des moyens ciblés pour protéger les données critiques et développer les compétences d’avenir. Un programme national d’urgence prévoit la formation de 5 000 experts en intelligence artificielle par an et l’intégration de modules d’apprentissage dès le secondaire. Il prévoit aussi la création du réseau des instituts JAZARI, consacrés à la recherche appliquée en IA, en science des données et en calcul haute performance. Un Cloud souverain national, reposant sur des centres de données sécurisés en territoire national, hébergera les données stratégiques de l’État et des opérateurs d’importance vitale, tandis que les systèmes de détection et de réponse aux cyberattaques seront mis à niveau. Le Programme prévoit enfin le renforcement de la prévention des catastrophes naturelles, avec la finalisation de la Stratégie nationale Risques 2030, qui couvre séismes, inondations et glissements de terrain. Il comprend le déploiement du dispositif Vigirisques Inondations, un système d’alerte précoce fondé sur des capteurs connectés et une modélisation hydrologique en temps réel, ainsi que l’opérationnalisation du Fonds de Solidarité contre les Événements Catastrophiques, destiné à indemniser les populations vulnérables et à accélérer la reconstruction. The post Énergie, eau, semences : la souveraineté érigée en doctrine appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Four-goal Roma thrash Yaya Toure’s Slovan Bratislava
items.description: Ruthless Roma stuck four past Yaya Toure’s Slovan Bratislava to secure their first Champions League victory of the season. Goals from Mario Hermoso, Nahuel Molina, Niccolo Pisilli and Donyell Malen sparked the Serie A side’s European campaign into life on what is their return to the competition for the first time since 2019. Roma suffered a shocking late collapse last week to lose 4-3 against Real Madrid as they conceded three goals in the last seven minutes. But they bounced back here and were in front against the Slovakian side inside 21 minutes when Hermoso headed in almost on the goal-line after Daniele Ghilardi nodded down Lorenzo Pellegrini’s free-kick. Roma were dominant against the side managed by former Manchester City midfielder Toure and got a deserved second six minutes before the break. Molina forced the ball home at the back post for his first goal for the club after Brastislava keeper Dominik Takac pushed ex-Aston Villa forward Malen’s shot across goal. Roma, who drew their opening European game of the season against Fenerbahce, took advantage of some hesitant defending early in the second half to get their third. Matias Soule managed to win the ball in the area before Malen played the ball back for Pisilli to turn home in the 52nd minute. Malen then got the fourth from the penalty spot just before the hour mark after Cesar Blackman fouled Wesley Franca to leave Toure’s side bottom of the Champions League table.

items.title: Nigeria confirms first Ebola case amid concerns about continental spread
items.description: Nigeria has confirmed its first Ebola case in its capital, Abuja, after a woman who travelled from Uganda tested positive for the virus. The case in the West African country comes amid an outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo and some cases in Kenya, raising concerns about a spread across the continent. According to Nigeria’s Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, the woman began showing symptoms on October 7 and was admitted to a private hospital in Abuja on October 11, before being diagnosed with Ebola. Health Minister Muhammad Pate said authorities had begun trying to trace 44 people who came into contact with the patient. “We are doing everything possible to contain this case by tracing all the contacts the individual may have had,” he said. New case in Kenya Earlier on Tuesday, Kenya confirmed ⁠its ninth case of Ebola. A 24-year-old man, who was already being held in quarantine, is the latest to test positive, Kenya’s Ministry of Health said in a statement on Tuesday. “He was isolated at the first sign of illness, tested and started on treatment immediately upon confirmation of his positive test result,” it said, adding he “was already in quarantine when he fell ill”. The man was a close family member of Kenya’s first Ebola patient , who had travelled from the DRC, through Uganda and before arriving in Kenya and dying at a Nairobi hospital on ⁠October 5. “All nine cases belong to one cluster, and as of ‌today there is no evidence of transmission outside this group,” Director-General for Health Patrick Amoth said in a statement on Tuesday. “Eight patients are stable and responding well to treatment, while 134 of 135 contacts have been traced and quarantined,” Amoth said. Amoth said a milestone was in sight for the majority of the contacts in quarantine as they had remained well for the 21-day monitoring period and could return home from October 25. It appealed to communities to welcome them back, saying they “pose no risk of infection”. The ministry said no infections had occurred within quarantine facilities and that it was continuously monitoring infection-prevention measures to protect health workers. Despite the nine infections, Kenya has not imposed restrictions on travel, trade or public gatherings, with authorities saying the country remains open for business. In the DRC, there have been more than 9,000 Ebola cases and 4,000 deaths since May. The European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control says it’s the second-largest epidemic on record. It has been difficult to contain because there is no licensed vaccine or specific treatment for the Bundibugyo strain of the virus. Uganda had previously reported Ebola cases but was later declared free of the virus.

items.title: Adansi group petitions chief to reopen Obuasi SHTS, reinstate 38 teachers
items.description: A group calling itself Concerned Citizens of Adansi has petitioned the Adansihene to intervene for the immediate reopening of Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS), which has remained closed for months following disturbances on campus. The school was shut down after the Ashanti Regional Education Directorate and the Obuasi Municipal Assembly ordered its closure following a riot in which students reportedly attacked the headmaster, Zakaria Abdulai, over allegations of sexual abuse involving female students. Abdulai is currently under investigation following a recent JoyNews exposé that further examined allegations of sexual encounters with about 19 girls at the school. The allegations have not been established, and investigations are ongoing. Despite the commencement of the new academic calendar in senior high schools, academic activities at Obuasi SHTS have yet to resume. In their petition, the concerned citizens said the closure had left Form Two and Form Three students at home without a clear timeline for returning to the classroom. “The situation is particularly alarming for Form Three students, who should be preparing intensively for their West African Senior School Certificate Examination (WASSCE). The loss of valuable instructional time threatens their examination preparation and academic prospects,” the statement said. The group said parents and guardians were increasingly distressed by the uncertainty surrounding their children’s education. “Our children must not become collateral victims of an administrative crisis. Their right to education and their prospects for academic success must not be sacrificed while the relevant authorities deliberate over the issues surrounding the school,” it added. Group questions reported dismissal of 38 teachers The group also expressed concern over the reported dismissal of 38 teachers from the school following criticism of the handling of allegations involving the headmaster. It said the reports raised questions about administrative accountability, procedural fairness and the protection of teachers who raise concerns about developments within their institution. “We acknowledge that the allegations require independent verification. Nevertheless, we are deeply concerned that the reported transfers could create a perception of victimisation and divert public attention from the substantive issues that require investigation,” the statement said. “The displacement of teachers must not become a substitute for establishing the truth, nor should innocent educators suffer professional consequences for raising legitimate concerns.” Calls for impartial investigation The concerned citizens are appealing to traditional authorities to intervene to secure the reopening of the school. They are also demanding an impartial investigation into the allegations against the headmaster and the circumstances surrounding the reported directive affecting the teachers. The group said resolving the issues was necessary to protect students’ education while ensuring that the allegations and concerns raised by staff were addressed through a fair process.

items.title: Carrick wants more clean sheets to turn season around
items.description: “You’re dead right. I can’t argue with that.” Michael Carrick’s response was to the point. The question that prompted it in his pre-match news conference at a rain-lashed Giuseppe Sinigaglia stadium in Como concerned his side’s failure to keep clean sheets. Carrick was asked whether it would help if United could manage some shutouts, and whether he had figured out the problem. United have kept the opposition out just once in 10 games this season, against Azerbaijan champions Sabah FK last month. “There’s definitely parts of our game we have to improve to make things easier. I am fully aware of that,” said Carrick, whose side take on Como in the Champions League on Wednesday. The problem goes further than this season, though. They managed six clean sheets in Carrick’s 17 matches in charge last term, including two in their final three games. Prior to that, they had only managed two all season, part of an overall tally of nine in 63 games under his predecessor Ruben Amorim. It is an extreme comparison given solid defence was the bedrock of Arsenal’s Premier League title triumph, but the Gunners, who face Bayern Munich in Germany on Wednesday, have recorded seven clean sheets in 11 matches this season. Fulham’s Josh King celebrates Lisandro Martinez’s own goal at Craven Cottage on 20 September Continuity of selection would presumably help Carrick achieve defensive stability. It has proved virtually elusive so far. Only once has Carrick been able to name the same back four: Diogo Dalot, Harry Maguire, Lisandro Martinez and Luke Shaw started the victory against Ipswich at Old Trafford on 30 August and kept their places for the trip to Everton the following week. Carrick described his fitness update before the Como encounter as “a mixed bag”. That was largely based on him saying Netherlands defender Matthijs de Ligt was “fit and ready” after 11 months on the sidelines with the back injury that required surgery in May. Yet De Ligt was on the bench at Leeds on Sunday when Martinez went off with the thigh injury that prevented him travelling to Italy, and instead Carrick turned to Noussair Mazraoui, usually a full-back, for the central slot. United’s defensive resources are stretched thinner as Leny Yoro is ruled out through suspension. Shaw is still not fit and is expected to be out for “a little bit longer” than the 10 days Kobbie Mainoo is going to miss, which could mean the left-back won’t return until after the November international break. Will Amass be the sixth left-back this season? Diogo Dalot became the fifth different player to start for Manchester United at left-back this season at Leeds – and Harry Amass could become the sixth To many observers, the Manchester United left-back situation was predictable and should have been addressed in the summer. United speaking to Manchester City about Algeria international Rayan Ait-Nouri on deadline day suggests they saw it as a potential issue. After starting all 38 Premier League games last term and the first three this, Shaw has played only twice since, and the number of games missed could reach double figures before the 31-year-old returns. When Diogo Dalot lined up at left-back against Leeds, he became the fifth different player to start there for United in six games. Aside from Shaw, none of the quintet was a natural left-back. However, after it was suggested Martinez’s post-match outburst following the defeat by Atletico Madrid was partly down to 20-year-old Ayden Heaven playing at left-back, sources did point out the youngster played more often in that role than in the centre during his youth days at Arsenal. In the summer, United’s coaching team also suggested they did not believe 19-year-old Harry Amass, Shaw’s stand-in during pre-season, was yet at the right level. Amass’ single appearance so far this season, as a substitute for the final 18 minutes against Sabah, backs up that view, although Carrick has countered it. “He’s right in contention,” Carrick said. “At some point, young players need an opportunity. It’s just finding the right time. “Sometimes it’s because there’s an unfortunate thing that happened to somebody else. Sometimes it’s just that you’re doing so well we have to give you a chance. “All the young players are in a similar boat. There’s maybe four, five, or six of them trying to make that next step in terms of getting into the team and trying to start games, and Harry’s definitely one of them.” We made best of transfer window – Carrick Manchester United chief executive Omar Berrada (right), next to sporting director Jason Wilcox (second right) The failure to sign competition for Shaw is a stick used to beat Carrick and sporting director Jason Wilcox. Sympathy runs through the agent fraternity for Wilcox, who was given a budget that many in the game felt was inadequate to address United’s needs. Some believe the £50m spent to sign Andrey Santos from Chelsea should have gone elsewhere. With Santos sitting next to him as he spoke to the media on Tuesday, Carrick was hardly going to engage with that topic. “When we’ve got injuries at different stages, we can always look at what could have been done and where we could have improved,” Carrick said. “I spoke to you about making the best of the transfer window in the situation we had. This man next to us [Santos] was a big part of that. I’m delighted to have him. “We had to make decisions in the summer. We did what we could do and made the best of it.”

items.title: Six Nigerians listed as NBA sets Africa-player record for 2026-27
items.description: By Emmanuel Okogba The National Basketball Association (NBA) has announced a record number of players born in Africa or with at least one parent born on the continent on opening-night rosters for the 2026-27 season, with six Nigerian players listed among the international contingent. According to the league, more than 60 players with African backgrounds feature on opening-night rosters, while the overall number of international players stands at 125 from 43 countries across six continents. The NBA said this marks the sixth consecutive season with at least 120 international players and the 13th straight season with at least 100. The six players listed under Nigeria are Ugonna Onyenso of the Detroit Pistons, Charles Bassey of the Golden State Warriors, Adem Bona of the Philadelphia 76ers, Precious Achiuwa of the Sacramento Kings, Josh Okogie of the Utah Jazz and Felix Okpara of the Washington Wizards. The league also reported that more than 25 of the players with African backgrounds have Nigerian connections, including those born elsewhere or with at least one parent from Nigeria. Among the prominent players with Nigerian heritage are Miami Heat star Bam Adebayo, New York Knicks forward OG Anunoby and Milwaukee Bucks forward Giannis Antetokounmpo. The African-connected group also includes Philadelphia 76ers centre Joel Embiid and Indiana Pacers forward Pascal Siakam, both of whom were born in Cameroon. The NBA said France leads the international player count with 17, followed by Canada with 16. Australia has nine players, Germany seven, while Nigeria and Serbia have six each. France’s representation is led by San Antonio Spurs star Victor Wembanyama, the reigning NBA Defensive Player of the Year. Canada’s contingent includes Oklahoma City Thunder guard Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, the reigning two-time NBA Most Valuable Player. The Dallas Mavericks, Miami Heat and Washington Wizards have the highest number of international players among NBA teams, with seven each. All 30 franchises have at least one international player on their opening-night rosters. The league also recorded 70 European players for the season, marking the second consecutive campaign with at least that number. International players have continued to make their mark on the NBA’s individual awards. According to the league, four international stars have shared the last eight Most Valuable Player awards: Gilgeous-Alexander, Nikola Jokić, Joel Embiid and Giannis Antetokounmpo. Last season also marked the fifth consecutive campaign in which three international players finished among the top three in MVP voting, with Gilgeous-Alexander first, Jokić second and Wembanyama third. The NBA further announced that a record 19 international players who have previously been named All-Stars are on opening-night rosters for the 2026-27 season. More than 45 players on the rosters have also participated in Basketball Without Borders, the NBA and International Basketball Federation’s global basketball development and community outreach programme. The 2026-27 campaign is the NBA’s 81st regular season. The league said its games would reach fans in 214 countries and territories in more than 50 languages through broadcast partners and NBA League Pass. The record African representation and Nigeria’s six-player contingent underscore the continued presence of Nigerian talent in the NBA as the league expands its international reach. items.title: Specsavers founders get lifetime retail award
items.description: Specsavers’ founders have been given a lifetime award for their role in “transforming access to optical and audiology care”. Douglas and Dame Mary Perkins started the multinational company in Guernsey on a table-tennis table in their spare bedroom in 1984. The company now has more than 2,600 stores in 11 countries. They received the Lifetime Contribution Award at the Retail Gazette Awards last week, which honours people shaping the industry’s future. Dame Mary said she was “genuinely surprised” to receive the award, and described it as a “real honour to be recognised”. She said: “It’s a real honour to be recognised by the industry, especially as Doug and I approach 60 years in optics. “What makes it even more special is knowing that Specsavers has only ever been possible because of the passion and commitment of our partners and colleagues. “They’ve helped shape the business from day one and continue to make a difference for our customers every day.”

items.title: EBOLA: FAAN urges calm, vigilance among airport users
items.description: By Dickson Omobola Following the confirmation of an Ebola Virus Disease case in the Federal Capital Territory, FCT, the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria, FAAN, has said it is working with the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention, NCDC, Port Health Services, the Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority, NCAA, and other relevant agencies to support ongoing containment efforts. FAAN urged passengers, airport users, airlines and other stakeholders to remain calm, vigilant and cooperative with health officials. Director of Public Affairs and Consumer Protection at FAAN, Henry Agbebire, in a statement, said the authority had maintained heightened vigilance across airport operations and would continue to coordinate with public health authorities. The statement reads: “The early identification of the case and commencement of contact tracing underscore the importance of established public health protocols, effective surveillance and inter-agency collaboration in responding to potential health threats. “FAAN is maintaining heightened vigilance across airport operations and will continue to coordinate with public health authorities, align its response with further guidance and support additional measures considered necessary to safeguard passengers, airport personnel and the wider public. “The authority urges passengers, airport users, airlines and other stakeholders to remain calm, vigilant and cooperative with health officials. The public is also advised to rely on verified information and avoid spreading unconfirmed reports. “FAAN reassures the travelling public of its continued readiness to work with relevant agencies to protect public health and support the safe operation of Nigeria’s airports.” The post EBOLA: FAAN urges calm, vigilance among airport users appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman wins dismissal of sister’s lawsuit
items.description: OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman has won a dismissal of a lawsuit brought against him by his sister that claimed he had sexually abused her more than two decades ago. A US district judge dismissed the case after Ann Altman refused to attend an independent medical examination, adding that she was warned that failing to do so would result in the case being thrown out. Ann Altman had claimed the OpenAI founder had regularly sexually abused her between 1997 and 2006. Sam Altman has denied those accusations. The Altman family has said Ann Altman has mental health challenges and they have supported her financially, adding the claims were made as she continued to demand more funds. District Judge Zachary Bluestone said that despite multiple accommodations and opportunities, Ann Altman did not appear for an independent medical exam on three separate occasions and “failed to meaningfully prosecute her case”. “Because Annie has continued to violate her discovery obligations and forced this case to a halt through her intransigence, the Court has run out of options and, thus, dismisses her claims with prejudice,” he said in his written order. The case was filed on 6 January 2025 in the Eastern District of Missouri. In it, Ann Altman claimed that her older brother Sam Altman began abusing her when she was three, and he was 12. However, in a joint statement released by Sam Altman along with his mother and two brothers at the time, the family said they were concerned for Ann Altman’s well-being and had spent years trying to support her financially and look after her well-being. The family said she receives monthly financial support, and her bills and rent are covered, while they also try to help with medical care. The statement said her claims against Sam Altman changed drastically over time, but all of them were “utterly untrue”. Sam Altman is the co-founder of OpenAI, which launched its popular ChatGPT artificial intelligence chatbot in 2022.

items.title: Ligue des champions : le PSG fait plier le Barça
items.description: Le Paris Saint-Germain a signé une victoire de prestige face au FC Barcelone (4-2), mardi soir, au Parc des Princes, lors de la troisième journée de la phase de ligue de la Ligue des champions. Menés à deux reprises dans une rencontre riche en rebondissements, les Parisiens ont fait la différence en fin de match grâce à Vitinha et Fabián Ruiz. Le Paris Saint-Germain a remporté le choc face au FC Barcelone (4-2), mardi 20 octobre, au Parc des Princes. Dans une rencontre marquée par six buts, le club parisien a su répondre aux offensives catalanes pour décrocher un succès important dans la course à la qualification. Désiré Doué a ouvert le score pour les Parisiens à la 38e minute, récompensant la domination de son équipe en première période. Au retour des vestiaires, le Barça a réagi grâce à Xavi Espart, qui a égalisé à la 55e minute. Le PSG a repris l’avantage à la 72e minute sur une réalisation de Lucas Hernandez, avant que Lamine Yamal ne remette les deux équipes à égalité à la 79e minute. L’attaquant barcelonais a ainsi relancé le suspense, mais la réponse parisienne a été immédiate. Deux minutes après l’égalisation catalane, Vitinha a redonné l’avantage au PSG à la 81e minute. Fabián Ruiz a ensuite scellé le sort de la rencontre à la 86e minute, permettant aux champions d’Europe de s’imposer sur le score de 4-2. Cette victoire confirme la capacité du club parisien à répondre présent dans les grandes affiches européennes. Pour le FC Barcelone, cette défaite constitue un coup d’arrêt après un début de saison jusque-là convaincant. Avec ce succès, le PSG poursuit sa campagne européenne et envoie un signal fort à ses concurrents dans cette phase de ligue de la Ligue des champions.

items.title: PSG late show downs Barca in Champions League, Liverpool fight back
items.description: Holders Paris Saint-Germain made it three wins from three in this season’s Champions League, beating Barcelona 4-2 thanks to late goals from Vitinha and Fabian Ruiz on Tuesday, while Liverpool clinched a dramatic comeback victory over Villarreal. Phil Foden scored a hat-trick as Manchester City thrashed AEK Athens 5-1, while there were also much-needed wins for Roma and Napoli. PSG kept their place at the top of the early league-phase table, but could yet count the cost of injuries suffered by Ousmane Dembele, Marquinhos and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia at the Parc des Princes. Barcelona twice levelled against the two-time defending champions, but were ultimately well beaten as they slipped to their first defeat of the season. Hansi Flick’s men had won their previous 11 games in all competitions this term. Kvaratskhelia hit the post, Dembele hobbled off and Ferran Torres was denied by Barca goalkeeper Joan Garcia in a fast-paced opening. PSG took a deserved lead in the 38th minute as Desire Doue collected the ball outside the area and thumped a shot into the bottom corner. Garcia made another excellent save shortly after the break from Achraf Hakimi, before Xavi Espart burst through to level for Barca against the run of play. Kvaratskhelia and Marquinhos both pulled up injured within seconds of each other and had to leave the field. The home team continued to press, though, and Lucas Hernandez restored their advantage 18 minutes from time with a brilliant header, shortly after former Barcelona forward Torres hit the post. Lamine Yamal powered past Warren Zaire-Emery to equalise again seven minutes later. But Vitinha hammered home from outside the box in the 81st minute and Ruiz’s tap-in gave Luis Enrique’s team a second straight 4-2 Champions League win after seeing off Man City by the same scoreline last week. – Liverpool fight back – Liverpool battled back from two goals down to also maintain their 100-percent record by edging out Villarreal 4-3 at Anfield. Liverpool fell behind in the fourth minute when Georges Mikautadze pounced on a terrible error from Virgil van Dijk, before Villarreal defender Sergi Cardona strolled through their defence to make it two. Alexis Mac Allister pulled one back for the hosts nine minutes before half-time by heading in Kostas Tsimikas’s corner. Andoni Iraola’s men were level in first-half added time through Ronald Araujo’s back-post header after Cardona inexplicably left Rio Ngumoha’s cross. Mac Allister completed the turnaround by firing in from Ngumoha’s square pass, and half-time substitute Florian Wirtz’s first goal of the season gave the Reds some breathing space. Tani Oluwaseyi set up a nervy finish for Iraola, but Liverpool held on. At the Etihad, Elliot Anderson put Manchester City in front with his first goal for the club, tapping in a 12th-minute opener after Enzo Fernandez’s free-kick bounced back off the crossbar. Phil Foden made it two goals in as many games after scoring against Ipswich at the weekend, but AEK halved the deficit early in the second half through Stavros Pilios. Rayan Cherki capped a fine individual performance by sweeping in City’s third in the 57th minute. Foden later fired in his second and third goals in a comprehensive victory, despite Erling Haaland being rested after picking up a knock at the weekend. – Respite for Serie A clubs – Roma eased to their first Champions League win since 2019 as the capital club brushed aside pointless Slovan Bratislava 4-0 at the Stadio Olimpico. All four Serie A clubs in the competition lost last week, but Napoli made it two wins from two on Tuesday for the Italian sides. Massimiliano Allegri’s men were twice pegged back by Bodo/Glimt but eventually got the better of the Norwegians in a 4-3 thriller, as Scott McTominay scored a brace. Atletico Madrid played out a 1-1 draw with Stuttgart in Germany, despite playing much of the second half with 10 men. Borussia Dortmund ended a run of four straight away defeats in the Champions League with a 2-1 win over Sabah in Baku. Fenerbahce suffered another setback after last week’s humiliating 6-0 loss at Aston Villa, blowing a two-goal lead to be held 2-2 at home by Slavia Prague. PSV Eindhoven clinched their first victory with a 1-0 success at Porto. The post PSG late show downs Barca in Champions League, Liverpool fight back appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Trump sued over Canadian tariffs in latest legal challenge
items.description: US President Donald Trump faces another tariff-related legal challenge after the group that successfully sued over his so-called “liberation day” import taxes filed a new lawsuit over the latest Canadian levies. The White House imposed a 50% levy on some $20bn of Canadian goods after trade talks between the US and Canada broke down in August. The Liberty Justice Centre filed a suit on behalf of US food business Gellert Global Group, urging the US Court of International Trade to find the levies unlawful and to order refunds with interest for affected importers. The lawsuit argues the White House exceeded its authority in imposing the tariffs and caused “immediate harm to American businesses”. The White House has been contacted for comment. Gellert Global Group is a third-generation family business that is paying 50% tariffs on cheese exported from Canada. The New Jersey-based firm is also facing retaliatory tariffs from Canada on American-made cheese it sells north of the border. Co-chief executive Thomas Gellert said the firm spent generations building relationships with food industry suppliers and customers. “These tariffs disrupt those relationships overnight and create costs and uncertainty that ripple through the entire supply chain,” he said on Tuesday. The Liberty Justice Centre is challenging the administration’s use of Section 338 of the 1930 Tariff Act to hit Canadian goods from wine to dairy products and hockey sticks. That section of the nearly 100-year-old Act aims to protect US businesses from foreign discrimination, but the legal group argues it does not allow the executive branch to “impose sweeping tariffs or import restrictions whenever a trade dispute arises”. The lawsuit seeks to challenge the White House’s reliance on retaliatory tariffs imposed by Canada to justify its own duties under Section 338. Canada has imposed a series of countermeasures against numerous US tariffs. Last month, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney matched the Section 338 US tariffs “dollar for dollar” after Trump imposed them for what he called “unequal treatment” of US cars, dairy and alcohol. It also points out that Section 338 requires a 30-day waiting period before levies can be imposed, but the tariff on products including cheese was added to the list just a week before tariff collection began. Sara Albrecht, chief executive of the Liberty Justice Centre, said the case was not about Trump himself but about the presidency. “No president should have the power to pull a dormant statute off the shelf and use it to impose sweeping tariffs or import bans without the limits Congress required,” she said. The lawsuit argues that Section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930 has been superseded by Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974. It also argues that if Section 338 still applies, the White House has not established the legal basis for the sweeping tariffs against Canada. “The case is not an objection to tariffs as such. It asks who has the power to impose them and whether the executive branch followed the law Congress wrote,” the Liberty Justice Centre said. The law group has also filed a motion for a preliminary injunction to block their collection. It is the fourth case the group has brought against Trump’s tariffs, including its successful challenge to the sweeping tariffs brought in under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA) that were struck down in February this year. Albrecht said the group had brought all the cases for the same reason: “The Constitution gives tariff power to Congress. The executive branch cannot keep moving the same policy from one statute to another and pretend the limits disappear”.

items.title: Veteran gospel musician Bernice Offei to be buried on November 14
items.description: Veteran Ghanaian gospel musician Bernice Offei will be buried on Saturday, November 14, 2026, with funeral activities scheduled to take place at the Legon Interdenominational Church (LIC) in Legon, Accra. The funeral arrangements include a remembrance night on Wednesday, November 11, ahead of the burial service and final funeral rites on November 14. The remembrance night will begin at 7:00 pm, with seating scheduled to start at 6:30 pm. On Saturday, November 14, filing past will take place from 7:00 am to 9:00 am, followed by the burial service from 9:00 am to 11:00 am. The interment will be private, while the final funeral rites will be held at the church after the burial service. A thanksgiving service is scheduled for Sunday, November 15, at 10:30 am at the same venue. The funeral announcement indicates that there will be no sitting after the memorial service. Background Bernice Offei died on Saturday, September 12, 2026, at the age of 63, after a career spanning several decades in Ghana’s gospel music industry. Her death was announced by fellow gospel musician Nii Okai, while music producer Kwasi Ernest also confirmed the news. Her passing came days after she had been reported missing in Accra on September 1. She was later found, bringing relief to her family and members of the public who had joined efforts to locate her. Her former manager, Kwasi Ernest, disclosed that she had battled dementia for about five years before her death. He said the condition affected her memory and ability to carry out everyday activities. Offei was widely known for gospel songs including Life Is Short , Hold On and Kaa She Gbeyei . Her contribution to Ghanaian gospel music was recognised at the 2009 Ghana Music Awards, where she won Best Female Vocal Performance and Songwriter of the Year. She leaves behind a musical legacy that inspired generations of gospel music lovers in Ghana and beyond.
