La ministre a ajouté, lors d’une intervention dans le cadre d’une rencontre ministérielle internationale sur l’intelligence artificielle et l’éducation, lundi en Italie, que la meilleure utilisation de ces technologies est celle qui contribue au développement des capacités de chaque enfant et qui répond à ses besoins éducatifs. Mint Babah a présenté l’expérience mauritanienne en matière d’utilisation des technologies modernes pour l’organisation des concours nationaux, ainsi que les efforts déployés pour explorer les possibilités de leur utilisation lors des examens. La ministre a souligné l’importance de former les enseignants et de veiller à ce que tous les élèves puissent bénéficier des opportunités offertes par ces technologies, tout en garantissant la protection des données personnelles. Elle a affirmé que l’enjeu principal consistait à utiliser l’intelligence artificielle pour construire une école plus équitable et de meilleure qualité, capable de développer les compétences des apprenants et de libérer leur potentiel créatif, appelant à renforcer la coopération internationale et l’échange d’expériences et de savoir-faire afin de tirer parti du potentiel de ces technologies pour le développement de l’éducation.

items.title: Tinubu mourns Afenifere leader Fasoranti
items.description: By Adeola Badru Afenifere has mourned its leader, Chief Reuben Famuyide Fasoranti, recalling his contributions to Nigeria’s independence struggle, opposition to military rule and the campaign for the restoration of the annulled June 12, 1993 presidential election, as it described him as an exemplary leader whose life embodied patriotism, courage and service to humanity. The pan-Yoruba socio-political organisation announced his passing in a statement issued on Tuesday by its National Publicity Secretary, Comrade Jare Ajayi, who said the centenarian, also known as Asiwaju Yoruba, died at about 4pm. Fasoranti, who turned 100 on May 11, 2026, was described by Afenifere as “a humanist, a philanthropist, an exemplary leader, a genuine patriot and a Yoruba leader and an icon” who remained a model of courage even in the most heart-rending circumstances. The organisation said the late elder statesman was the first of its leaders to attain the age of 100, having assumed the leadership of Afenifere in November 2008 following the death of his predecessor, Chief Abraham Adesanya, in August of the same year. According to the statement, Fasoranti followed in the footsteps of his predecessors by living an exemplary life from which individuals and organisations could draw inspiration and model their conduct. One of the frontline followers of the late Chief Obafemi Awolowo in the Action Group’s struggle for Nigeria’s independence, Fasoranti remained involved in progressive politics in the post-independence period. His lifetime spanned Nigeria’s colonial era, independence, the Civil War, successive military administrations and the return to democratic rule. Afenifere recalled that Fasoranti was actively involved in the National Democratic Coalition (NADECO), which spearheaded the struggle for the restoration of the June 12, 1993 presidential election won by the late Chief Moshood Kashimawo Olawale Abiola. The organisation said he participated actively in efforts to restore civilian rule whenever the military intervened in Nigeria’s political process, describing him as “a democrat par excellence”. It added that Fasoranti, like his political mentor, Awolowo, and his predecessors as Afenifere leader, the late Chief Adekunle Ajasin and Chief Abraham Adesanya, believed that public office should be used to serve the best interests of the people. Beyond his political engagements, the late elder statesman was an educationist who established Omolere Nursery and Primary School, Akure High School and St. Frances’ Academy in Igoba, Akure, Ondo State. He also served as Ondo State Commissioner for Finance between 1979 and 1983 under the administration of the late Governor Michael Adekunle Ajasin in the old Ondo State. Afenifere described Fasoranti as an unassuming progressive icon whose commitment to humanity, philanthropy and public service would continue to inspire individuals and organisations. The organisation said it would “sorely miss this exemplary, unassuming, progressive icon who was a humanist and philanthropist in every sense of it”. It extended its condolences to the deceased’s immediate and extended families, the Ondo State Government and people, members of the Afenifere family in Nigeria and the diaspora, the Yoruba people worldwide and Nigerians, noting that Nigeria was a country dear to Fasoranti. Il a précisé que la stratégie nationale pour la consolidation de la paix et de la cohésion sociale pour la période 2025-2030, adoptée par le Conseil des ministres le 31 décembre 2025, met l’accent sur la décentralisation, l’intégration territoriale, l’autonomisation économique des jeunes et des femmes, la gouvernance des ressources naturelles et la prévention de l’extrémisme. De son côté, le représentant résident de la Banque mondiale en Mauritanie, Ibou Diouf, a souligné l’importance de renforcer la coopération entre les deux parties, indiquant que cette rencontre constituait une occasion de discuter des réformes proposées dans le cadre du projet « Prévention et résilience », et insistant sur l’importance de la coopération dans les domaines de la paix et de la sécurité au vu des défis auxquels la région est confrontée.

items.title: FIFA U17 WWC: Flamingos beat Puerto Rico 2-0 to boost hopes
items.description: Nigeria’s U-17 women’s national team, the Flamingos, boosted their chances at the ongoing FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco after securing a 2-0 victory over Puerto Rico in their Group B encounter in Rabat on Tuesday. The Flamingos, who won bronze at the 2022 edition of the competition, took the lead in the 25th minute through striker Oluwakemi Adegbuyi, who converted a pass from Queen Joseph. Nigeria started brightly, applying pressure on Puerto Rico’s defence and creating opportunities through quick passing and forward movement. Adegbuyi’s goal rewarded the team’s early efforts and gave Nigeria greater control of the game as the first half progressed. The Nigerian side continued to search for a second goal after the break, with Queen Joseph, Tosin Rafiu and Favour Nkwocha among those who threatened the Puerto Rican defence. Puerto Rico attempted to respond with tactical changes, but Nigeria coach Hakeem Busari also made substitutions to strengthen his team’s attacking options. Awawu Bashiru and Oluebube Umejiaku were introduced in the 67th minute as the Flamingos maintained their push for another goal. Their efforts paid off in the 90th minute when substitute Precious Oscar headed home a cross from Kemi Adegbuyi to double Nigeria’s lead and secure the victory. The Flamingos held on through six minutes of added time to claim all three points and strengthen their position in Group B. In the other group fixture, North Korea defeated Poland 6-1, setting up an important encounter with Nigeria on Friday. The result against Puerto Rico gives the Flamingos a boost ahead of the meeting with North Korea, which could prove crucial to their progress in the tournament. items.title: You Can Believe Everything
items.description: It was fitting that, just hours after the first public screenings of the Elizabeth Holmes documentary began last Thursday, Elon Musk put on a show of his own. That night, in Texas, Musk unveiled the company’s new Roadster prototype, a car that would defy gravity. Tesla built what was roughly one-half of a roller-coaster loop, which the Roadster climbed before momentarily hanging upside down and then executing a controlled flip and gliding down to Earth. The demo worked. In another stunt, it did a barrel roll over a semi-truck. Each maneuver was powered by air thrusters that guided the car to a soft landing. The demo was impressive. But watching the clips, I could feel my brain struggling to process what I was being shown. Was this real? The car did climb vertically, flip, and land. But Musk, who has built wildly successful companies, is also famously prone to outlandish claims that don’t always pan out. I couldn’t help but wonder what, if anything, Tesla’s demonstration or Musk had elided. “This will be an actual car that’s on the roads,” Musk said. He got the flying-car headlines he wanted, but will this car actually be released? There are already reasons to doubt it: The car displayed on Thursday won’t be in production until at least 2028, and it features 10 thrusters powered by 600 liters of compressed air. The flying version of the Roadster will be sold “invite-only.” Its price tag is likely to be astronomical. And so Musk isn’t exactly lying here. Rather, he’s making bold proclamations and asking people to take his pledge to deliver as an article of faith. [ Read: ] Imagine every AI agent on Earth buying the same cheap paper towels Less than 48 hours later, I found myself sitting in a crowded theater, watching the new documentary You Can See Everything , about the disgraced and convicted founder of Theranos, Elizabeth Holmes, and her husband, Billy Evans. In one scene, Holmes and Evans are hurriedly trying to court investors and research talent to build out what they refer to as Theranos 2.0. This scene is arguably the only time in the film where the duo don’t appear to be filled with existential dread. During phone calls and Zoom meetings, they spit out jargon and look earnestly excited about what they can build if they “get the band back together.” At the end of the sequence, Holmes is asked about why she’s spending her last days with her family building a company, and she responds that this is what she’s meant to be doing here on Earth. It is one of the few moments where I confidently believe her. Whatever she earnestly believes about her own guilt, it seems clear that her identity is inextricably tied to her notion that she is, in Silicon Valley parlance, a builder: a high-agency, visionary type with a remarkable risk tolerance who makes things and isn’t afraid to fail, because she has a monomaniacal obsession with pushing the bounds of what’s possible. The film, which had the biggest opening for a documentary in more than 20 years, is extremely well suited to a post-truth era. The co-directors, Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, bury the audience with unreliable narration such that, when you get to the end, you feel like a participant in the film. It also left me exhilarated, slightly repulsed, and feeling as if I was going insane. In that way, the documentary replicates what it’s like to navigate the informational hall of mirrors we all inhabit. But what I found most bracing about the film—more so than the supposed unknowability of anyone or anything—is how Holmes’s act and affect do not feel like an aberration in 2026. In fact, her behavior embodies the current ethos of Silicon Valley. When she built Theranos, Holmes was a college dropout with boundless ambitions who styled herself after Steve Jobs. Jobs famously said things such as “People don’t know what they want until you show it to them,” and Holmes, like Jobs, projected the aura of a person ready to pull the future into the present by any means necessary. Jobs routinely delivered on these promises, and kept many projects secret until they were ready for the masses. Holmes did the opposite, offering a fantastical version of a product that did not exist, obscuring the actual capabilities and lying about the financials. She wasn’t alone; over time, the idea of the builder became more synonymous with a founder’s ideas, charisma, and salesmanship than with the products themselves. “I watched countless founders of hard tech companies present fraudulent products at conferences,” Nikita Bier, a tech entrepreneur who was recently Elon Musk’s head of product at X, wrote on the platform this weekend in response to the documentary. “They had fake studies with fudged numbers. Most of the adults in the room excused it as ‘faking it ‘til you make it.’” Holmes’s high-profile failure and the collapse of Theranos in 2018 didn’t kill the builder archetype. If anything, the very structure of Silicon Valley became more deeply intertwined with the builder mindset. Fake it ’til you make it (provided it isn’t outright fraud) is a necessary outcome of an industry that’s funded by venture capitalists, who often make strategic bets on projects so early in development that the products are still hypothetical. And so VCs threw unfathomable money at promising but half-baked ideas in the hopes of fabulous payouts. Failures were overlooked, even celebrated as necessary or teachable moments—honorable proof of being a “man in the arena.” In 2022, after Sam Bankman-Fried’s crypto empire was revealed to be an elaborate Ponzi scheme, the writer John Ganz argued that, in an industry built on big bets, the line between frauds and visionaries becomes difficult to suss out until everything implodes. “This is the Fyre Festival era of capitalism: outlandish promises and then a ludicrous debacle.” Much of that rush to invest has been driven by a culture progressively gripped by the fear of missing out on the next industry-shaking payout. Untold billions were poured into crypto, then NFTs, Web3, and the ill-fated metaverse. In crypto, rug-pulling scams and Ponzi schemes abounded; its boosters said things such as “Have fun staying poor.” Today we’re living through what many suggest could be an AI bubble, and the same mentality persists. Have fun staying poor has been replaced with the idea of a “permanent underclass” of people who failed to get in early and now stand to lose their economic viability, and potentially their human agency altogether. Like Theranos, crypto, and NFTs, the AI industry is defined by claims of its inevitability and its future power (to be certain, chatbots and coding agents are real and powerful in ways the other technologies were not). In this way, AI is a faith-based technology; one’s desire to work on it, bet the success of the global economy on it, love it, or fear its End Times powers is typically predicated on what one can imagine it might become. The past eight years have warped the tech industry to the point that it can feel untethered from the constraints of reality. You can see it in headlines everywhere if you’re looking. On Saturday, an Anthropic co-founder, Jack Clark, suggested that the U.S. GDP could jump in the next four years from about $30 trillion to $44 trillion thanks to rapid AI-driven progress in many industries. This would be one of the largest periods of growth in U.S. history, a prediction based on nothing more than the most “extreme parameter setting” of an Anthropic economic model the company released this fall. You can see it in the IPO prospectuses for a company like SpaceX, which includes in its ambitions the goal to “extend the light of consciousness to the stars” and initiatives such as asteroid mining and space tourism. And earlier this month, Musk noted that “this will sound super crazy, but I see a path to SpaceX being worth orders of magnitude more than the current Earth economy.” You could call all these claims tech optimism or, as the famed venture capitalist Marc Andreessen wrote in his 2023 manifesto , necessary for the “glory of human ambition and achievement, the spearhead of progress, and the realization of our potential.” You could also call it speculative fiction. About halfway through the film, Holmes heads to prison and the documentary shifts to focus on Billy Evans, the man with whom Holmes has two children. With Holmes in prison, Evans has become her unreliable narrator. He is, as others have noted, also a helpful lens to understand the transformation of Silicon Valley. Evans has seemingly embraced Musk and Andreessen’s brand of vice signaling . We see him shooting guns, extolling Charlie Kirk, and lashing out at people on X under the cloak of anonymity (posting as Holmes, using her X account). He makes grandiose claims about his new company but seems embittered and incapable of submitting to hard questions about it. The veneer of excitement that the couple project in the Theranos 2.0 montage is replaced by a paranoia and resentment that people, including possibly Fielder, might be trying to take him down. It all made me wonder how Silicon Valley might respond to Theranos’s collapse if it were happening today. Reactionary types in the industry might rally around Holmes, insisting that she was too early or needed more time. They might attack the press more forcefully for trying to bring her down (Holmes and Theranos did try to retaliate against whistleblowers and the reporter who broke the story). Trust in traditional media is even lower now than it was back then, and Silicon Valley has a robust ecosystem of very popular, industry-friendly podcasts and creators who could champion Holmes’s narrative. Evans, for instance, appeared last week on the popular All-In podcast. X is now owned by Musk. The truth takes longer to come out; in some cases, it might feel almost irrelevant. The universal outrage that Theranos sparked in 2015, when news first emerged that something was deeply wrong, sounds quaint now. “When people ask how she got so far, it’s largely explained by the period she did it in,” Bier wrote in his X post about Holmes. “And she got caught when the world suddenly woke up.” I agree with the first part of Bier’s statement and take issue with the second. The brand of delusion that defined Holmes and the twisted epistemological game that You Can See Everything showcases is still deeply embedded in the industry. None of this is to suggest that everyone in Silicon Valley is engaged in rampant, Theranos-like provable fraud. But today’s entrepreneurs are emboldened to make even more outlandish claims about the future, and it’s more difficult than ever to parse what is real, what is knowingly fake, and what is being offered in good or bad faith. In response to Bier’s post, Jason Calacanis, an investor and a co-host of All-In , noted that there was “much truth” to Bier’s explanation before he offered a rebuttal befitting a true builder—AI will soon solve the Theranos problem: “In the next ten years, a blood testing product will emerge that will make folks go, ‘See, @ElizabethHolmes was just 20 years too early!’” The builder is never wrong. If anything, they are just early. The future is coming. Just have faith. *Illustration sources: Justin Sullivan / Getty; Liesa Johannssen-Koppitz / Bloomberg / Getty; Tayfun Coskun / Anadolu / Getty; USA Today / Reuters.

items.title: Participation mauritanienne à Astana à la semaine de la sécurité aérienne de l’OACI
items.description: L'Agence nationale de l'aviation civile de Mauritanie a participé ce mardi, à Astana, la capitale du Kazakhstan, aux événements de la Semaine de la sécurité aérienne de l'OACI 2026 (ICAO Security Week 2026), organisée par l'Organisation de l'aviation civile internationale (OACI). L'Agence était représentée lors de ce forum par son directeur général, Baba Ahmed Mohamed Baba Ahmed, et par le directeur de la sécurité et des facilités de l'Agence, Oumar Mokhtar. L'Agence a déclaré sur sa page Facebook que sa participation à cet événement international constituait une occasion importante d'échanger des connaissances et des expériences entre les États et les organismes compétents dans le domaine de la sécurité de l'aviation civile. Le forum passe en revue les dernières évolutions et les défis en matière de sécurité auxquels est confronté le secteur du transport aérien, tout en examinant les moyens de renforcer les systèmes de sécurité aérienne et de développer les procédures de protection et les facilités, conformément aux normes et pratiques internationales en vigueur. Cette participation revêt une importance particulière dans le cadre des préparatifs de la Mauritanie en vue des prochains rendez-vous internationaux dans le domaine de la sécurité de l’aviation civile, au premier rang desquels figure l’audit de sécurité prévu par l’Organisation de l’aviation civile internationale (OACI) en 2027, auquel sera soumis le système national de sécurité de l’aviation civile, afin d’évaluer sa conformité aux normes internationales en vigueur dans ce domaine.

items.title: Trade Minister engages cement and battery firms to boost local manufacturing and jobs
items.description: The Minister for Trade, Agribusiness and Industry, Elizabeth Ofosu-Adjare, has engaged three companies in the cement, battery and renewable energy sectors on measures to strengthen local manufacturing, increase the use of Ghanaian raw materials and create jobs. The engagements, held on Tuesday, October 20, 2026, involved CIMPOR Cement Africa, Huaguang New Energy Battery Ghana and Zema New Energy Limited. At a meeting with CIMPOR Cement Africa Chief Executive Officer, Yasin Tekinarslan, discussions centred on tax relief for the local production and use of calcined clay to reduce the country’s dependence on imported clinker. The Minister welcomed initiatives that use locally available raw materials to support the production of affordable housing and help address Ghana’s housing deficit. The proposed use of calcined clay could support efforts to reduce reliance on imported materials in cement production, while promoting the utilisation of Ghanaian resources. Mrs Ofosu-Adjare also engaged Huaguang New Energy Battery Ghana on workers’ welfare and quality standards, reaffirming the government’s commitment to supporting local manufacturing. During a separate meeting with Zema New Energy Limited, a producer of solar photovoltaic cells, the Minister urged greater local participation in the company’s operations. She said stronger local participation would help promote job creation and business growth. The engagements form part of the Ministry’s efforts to strengthen domestic industry, encourage the use of local raw materials and expand opportunities for Ghanaian businesses and workers.

items.title: 61 Ghanaian nurses officially welcomed to Grenada
items.description: Sixty-one Ghanaian nurses have been officially welcomed to Grenada following their arrival in the Caribbean country to contribute to its healthcare delivery. The nurses received an official welcome ceremony on October 16, 2026, marking a significant milestone in their international professional journey. The ceremony celebrated their arrival and recognised the contribution they are expected to make to healthcare services in Grenada. Their arrival marks a new chapter in their professional careers as they take up opportunities to work outside Ghana and contribute their skills and experience to the country’s healthcare sector. Background Ghana and Grenada signed a memorandum of understanding on health cooperation in October 2025 to facilitate the recruitment of Ghanaian nurses for employment in the Caribbean country. The agreement followed discussions between President John Dramani Mahama and Grenadian Prime Minister Dickon Mitchell on strengthening bilateral relations, including cooperation in healthcare. Grenada expressed interest in recruiting Ghanaian nurses and allied health professionals to help address shortages in its healthcare system. The partnership forms part of Ghana’s broader Labour Export Programme, which seeks to expand international employment opportunities for skilled Ghanaians while supporting workforce needs in partner countries. The government has urged the deployed workers to demonstrate competence, discipline and professionalism to sustain such opportunities for other Ghanaian professionals.

items.title: JOJ Dakar 2026 : la Gendarmerie nationale mobilisée pour la sécurité
items.description: Le ministre des Forces armées, Yankoba Diémé, a effectué, mardi, une visite de plusieurs sites de compétition des Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse (JOJ) Dakar 2026, en compagnie du Haut-commandant de la Gendarmerie nationale, le général de division Martin Faye. Cette visite a permis d’examiner les préparatifs sécuritaires et le rôle opérationnel de la Gendarmerie nationale dans l’organisation de cet événement international. La visite visait notamment à apprécier l’état de préparation des sites de compétition, à identifier les enjeux sécuritaires liés aux Jeux et à évaluer le niveau d’implication de la Gendarmerie nationale dans le dispositif opérationnel. Elle devait également contribuer au renforcement de la coordination entre les différents acteurs chargés de la sécurité. Les échanges ont porté sur la prévention des risques, la sécurisation des sites, la protection des personnes et des biens ainsi que le maintien de l’ordre public. La préparation de cet événement repose, selon le communiqué, sur une planification rigoureuse et une coordination étroite entre les Forces de défense et de sécurité, les services de l’État et le Comité d’organisation des Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse (COJOJ). À l’issue de la visite, Yankoba Diémé a réaffirmé l’engagement de son département à accompagner les préparatifs des JOJ Dakar 2026, dans le cadre de ses attributions et en concertation avec les parties prenantes. La mobilisation des Forces de défense et de sécurité est présentée comme un élément essentiel à la sécurisation de cette compétition internationale, prévue au Sénégal.

items.title: Delayed funding of judiciary means delayed justice – Dr Valentine Mensah
items.description: Dr Valentine Mensah, D&D fellow in public financial management and corporate governance, has warned that delays in funding and inadequate resources are undermining effective justice delivery in Ghana. Speaking at a JoyNews and An Amalgam of Professionals event on Tuesday, October 20, he said the judiciary needed dependable financial support, adequate staffing, equipment and essential facilities to function effectively, stressing that accountability must be accompanied by the resources required for judges and court staff to perform their duties. “ We are paying people to work, but are we giving them the tools?” he asked, highlighting the imbalance between spending on personnel and investment in the operational needs of the courts. Dr Mensah cited figures indicating that Parliament approved GH¢945 million for the judiciary in 2024, but only GH¢700 million was released. Of the amount spent, compensation accounted for 79 per cent, leaving 21 per cent for goods, services and capital expenditure. “Delayed funding means delayed justice,” he said, arguing that government’s fiscal constraints, although understandable, should not result in prolonged delays in providing essential support to the courts. He said the situation persisted in 2025, when audited expenditure exceeded GH¢1.6 billion, with compensation absorbing 87 per cent and leaving only 13 per cent for other operational needs. According to him, the figures raise concerns about whether the judiciary has sufficient resources to provide the facilities and equipment needed for timely justice delivery. Dr Mensah cited the judicial complex, which he said had remained unfinished for more than a decade, as an example of how incomplete planning and funding delays could leave critical infrastructure unavailable. He also pointed to the Judicial Service’s internally generated funds of GH¢151 million in 2025, which he said represented about 15 per cent of its budget. He called for sustainable funding arrangements, including efficient fee collection and regular reviews of court fees, while protecting people who cannot afford to pay. On staffing, Dr Mensah referred to reports by the Judicial Service Staff Association of Ghana (JUSAG) that more than 130 courts were operating without magistrates. He said better conditions of service, improved security and timely recruitment are necessary to attract and retain qualified personnel. He further cited the Chief Justice’s report that 127 candidates had been interviewed but were awaiting clearance, leaving serving officers to cover multiple courts. Dr Mensah urged authorities to improve staffing plans, establish deadlines for recruitment clearances and provide explanations when appointments were delayed or refused. He also stressed that judicial independence required more than constitutional guarantees, arguing that judges needed adequate material support and security of tenure to make decisions without fear of political retaliation. While accountability remained essential, he said “procedures for removing judges must guarantee fair hearings, impartial adjudication and protection against political interference”. Articles 125 and 127 of Ghana’s 1992 Constitution establish the judiciary’s authority and protect its independence, reinforcing the need for institutional arrangements that enable the courts to discharge their responsibilities effectively. Dr Mensah said the judiciary’s challenges reflected wider problems in Ghana’s public sector, where the payment of salaries did not always translate into the provision of the tools and facilities needed to deliver public services. He called for all three arms of government to fulfil their constitutional responsibilities, noting that the Executive implements laws and policies, Parliament legislates and holds the government accountable, while the Judiciary interprets the law, protects rights and checks the exercise of public power. He said effective justice delivery was essential to protecting citizens against arbitrary power, enforcing contracts and creating an environment that supports investment and national development.

items.title: Obuasi SHTS headmaster arrested over sexual misconduct allegations – Muntaka
items.description: The Headmaster of Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS), Zakaria Abdulai, has been arrested in connection with sexual misconduct allegations involving female students, Interior Minister Mohammed Mubarak Muntaka has disclosed. Mr Muntaka made the disclosure when he appeared before Parliament’s Public Accounts Committee (PAC) on Tuesday, October 20, 2026. He said the case had been transferred from the regional level to Police Headquarters for further investigation after he directed that it be handled at the national level. According to the Minister, the matter came to his attention on September 7, when the Criminal Investigations Department (CID) received a report. He subsequently requested that the investigation be escalated to Police Headquarters. Mr Muntaka said investigators were pursuing DNA evidence as part of efforts to establish the facts surrounding the allegations. “We’ve been able to get one of the ladies, maybe I shouldn’t be putting so much information out, about semen, we are getting DNA… So, what is happening is that this gentleman has been arrested, He’s going through the due process,” the Minister said. He explained, however, that investigators would need a court order before collecting DNA samples, in accordance with the law. The arrest marks a development in investigations into the allegations against the headmaster, which have drawn public concern and calls for accountability. The allegations remain under investigation, and the arrest does not establish guilt.

Ligue des champions : le PSG prend le dessus sur le FC Barcelone
items.description: Au terme d’un match spectaculaire, le Paris Saint-Germain s’est imposé face au FC Barcelone sur le score de 4 buts à 2, dans le cadre de la Ligue des champions, face aux coéquipiers de Lamine Yamal. La rencontre a été marquée par une confrontation intense entre les deux équipes, dans un match au rythme soutenu et ponctué de nombreuses tentatives offensives de part et d’autre. Le club parisien a cherché à tirer profit de l’avantage du terrain et du soutien de son public pour imposer son style de jeu, tandis que l’équipe catalane a tenté de s’appuyer sur les qualités techniques de ses joueurs pour construire ses attaques et revenir au score, sous le regard d’un public particulièrement attentif à l’évolution de la rencontre. Le Paris Saint-Germain a réussi à prendre l’ascendant à plusieurs moments clés du match, en s’appuyant notamment sur la rapidité de ses transitions entre défense et attaque ainsi que sur son pressing exercé sur la défense barcelonaise. De son côté, le Barça a tenté de suivre le rythme de la rencontre et de trouver des espaces pour atteindre le but de l’équipe locale. L’efficacité offensive du club parisien a finalement fait la différence dans cette confrontation, qui a mis en évidence le potentiel offensif des deux équipes, mais aussi les difficultés défensives rencontrées par le club catalan. items.title: WCAF V : le SNAPE mise sur les investissements britanniques pour renforcer l’accès à l’eau potable en Guinée
items.description: À l’occasion de la 5ᵉ édition du UK–Francophone West & Central Africa Forum (WCAF V), consacrée au dialogue économique, au commerce, à l’investissement et au financement du développement entre le Royaume-Uni et les pays francophones d’Afrique de l’Ouest et du Centre, le directeur général du service national d’aménagement des points d’eau (SNAPE), Aladji Fodé Kaba, a mis en avant les opportunités offertes par cette rencontre pour renforcer les infrastructures hydrauliques en Guinée. S’exprimant en marge des travaux, il a souligné l’importance de ce forum pour attirer les investisseurs internationaux et mobiliser des financements en faveur du secteur de l’eau, notamment dans les zones rurales et semi-urbaines, où l’accès à l’eau potable demeure un défi. Pour lui (Aladji Fodé Kaba), le WCAF représente une vitrine permettant à la Guinée de valoriser son potentiel et de nouer des partenariats stratégiques avec des acteurs économiques étrangers. Il a également revendiqué un rôle dans l’initiative ayant conduit à l’organisation de cette édition en Guinée, évoquant des échanges avec le ministre du Plan et de la Coopération internationale, Ismaël Nabé, ainsi qu’avec l’ambassadeur de Guinée à Londres, lors d’un précédent forum organisé au Togo. « Le WCAF est une opportunité, parce que c’est une vitrine. Aujourd’hui, des investisseurs du monde entier sont présents pour essayer de tirer pleinement profit des opportunités qu’offre la Guinée », a-t-il déclaré, estimant que l’ouverture du pays aux investisseurs pouvait favoriser la concrétisation de projets structurants. Des adductions d’eau potable pour desservir les zones rurales Au-delà des opportunités économiques, le directeur général du SNAPE a particulièrement insisté sur les enjeux liés à l’approvisionnement en eau potable. Selon lui, les investissements envisagés doivent permettre de dépasser le modèle reposant essentiellement sur les forages, au profit de systèmes d’adduction capables d’alimenter plusieurs localités à partir d’infrastructures communes. Il a notamment cité Aqua Africa, une entreprise britannique disposant, selon lui, d’une expérience dans le domaine de l’hydraulique villageoise. Ces partenariats devraient contribuer à améliorer la desserte en eau des populations rurales, en facilitant l’installation de branchements directement dans les ménages. « Avec ces investissements, nous ne nous limitons plus aux forages : nous allons réaliser de grandes adductions d’eau potable », a expliqué Aladji Fodé Kaba, précisant que cette approche était déjà expérimentée à Koma, dans la préfecture de Kankan, ainsi qu’à Timbi-Madina. L’objectif, a-t-il poursuivi, est de permettre aux habitants des villages concernés de bénéficier d’un accès à l’eau comparable à celui des populations urbaines, sans avoir à parcourir de longues distances pour s’approvisionner. Les branchements domestiques, équipés de compteurs, devraient également contribuer à un meilleur suivi de la consommation. Pour lui, cette orientation traduit la volonté de faire évoluer les politiques d’approvisionnement en eau afin de mieux prendre en compte les besoins des communautés de l’intérieur du pays. Il a toutefois rappelé que la durabilité des infrastructures dépendrait de leur entretien. Plus d’un milliard d’euros évoqué pour soutenir les projets hydrauliques Dans son intervention, il a également évoqué un autre financement, qu’il a désigné sous le nom de « High-Tech », dont le montant dépasserait, selon ses déclarations, un milliard d’euros. Ce financement viendrait compléter les autres investissements présentés dans le cadre du forum. Il estime que la réalisation de ces différents projets pourrait contribuer à réduire considérablement les difficultés d’accès à l’eau potable dans les zones rurales et semi-urbaines. Il a toutefois souligné l’ampleur des besoins, qui concernent l’ensemble des régions naturelles du pays. « Si nous parvenons à réaliser l’ensemble de ces projets en milieu rural et semi-urbain, nous n’aurons plus de difficultés d’accès à l’eau dans ces zones », a-t-il affirmé, présentant l’amélioration de la desserte en eau des populations comme une priorité. Il a également rappelé les conséquences humaines du manque d’infrastructures hydrauliques. Il a notamment évoqué le cas de trois personnes d’une même famille qui auraient perdu la vie en allant chercher de l’eau en Guinée forestière. Selon lui, cette situation illustre l’urgence de renforcer les équipements permettant aux populations d’accéder à une eau potable de proximité. « Une telle situation est inacceptable au XXIe siècle », a-t-il déploré, appelant à une mobilisation accrue pour répondre aux besoins des communautés. Un défi qui concerne toutes les régions du pays Pour le patron du SNAPE, les difficultés d’accès à l’eau ne se limitent pas à la Guinée forestière. Elles concernent également la Haute-Guinée, la Moyenne-Guinée et la Basse-Guinée, où les besoins en infrastructures hydrauliques restent importants. Il a ainsi réaffirmé la volonté de son service de travailler à la réduction de ces insuffisances, en misant notamment sur les partenariats et les financements susceptibles d’être mobilisés à l’occasion du WCAF V. items.title: Ablakwa joins family, Ghanaian community to honour late Prof Jason Arday in UK
items.description: Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa has joined the family of the late Ghanaian academic Professor Jason Atta Kwei Arday, members of the Ghanaian community and British officials at a funeral service in Southwark, United Kingdom, to honour his life and legacy. The minister attended the service to pay tribute to Prof. Arday, whose achievements as the youngest Black professor appointed at the University of Cambridge and his charitable contributions continue to inspire people across the world. The service brought together Ghana’s High Commissioner to the UK, British Members of Parliament, ministers, the Mayor of London, Cambridge scholars, students of the late professor and other loved ones. In a statement highlighting the government’s participation, Mr Ablakwa said Ghana remained committed to supporting its citizens wherever they lived. He said the government and people of Ghana would continue to stand by their compatriots abroad while upholding the values of justice, equality and the creation of a better world. Prof. Arday was widely recognised for his academic achievements and contributions to social equality and inclusion. His life and work have continued to inspire generations, particularly through his commitment to widening opportunities and challenging barriers in education. The minister described the funeral service as deeply moving and unforgettable, paying tribute to the late professor’s vision of a more compassionate society. He recalled Prof. Arday’s response when asked what he would do to change the world. “I would take a thread and a needle, and I’d interweave love into our society,” the professor said. Mr Ablakwa also extended his condolences to the bereaved family, praying for strength and comfort for them during what he described as an extraordinarily difficult time.

Agriculture : le MASAE veut inscrire l’équité de genre dans les budgets et les programmes
items.description: Dix ans après la création de sa Cellule Genre, le ministère de l’Agriculture, de la Souveraineté alimentaire et de l’Élevage veut renforcer la prise en compte de l’équité de genre dans ses budgets et ses programmes. Lors d’un atelier tenu ce mardi 20 octobre à Diamniadio, le ministre Cheikhou Oumar Ba a appelé l’ensemble de ses services à traduire cet engagement en actions concrètes. La Cellule Genre et de l’Équité du ministère de l’Agriculture, de la Souveraineté alimentaire et de l’Élevage (MASAE) a organisé, mardi 20 octobre, à la Sphère ministérielle Ousmane Tanor Dieng de Diamniadio, un atelier de partage des résultats et de capitalisation des bonnes pratiques, avec l’appui du Programme agricole Italie-Sénégal (PAIS). En présidant la rencontre, le ministre Cheikhou Oumar Ba a reconnu les progrès accomplis depuis 2016, tout en insistant sur la nécessité de franchir une nouvelle étape. Selon lui, l’intégration du genre doit désormais se traduire dans les décisions quotidiennes, les outils de planification, les allocations budgétaires et l’exécution des programmes. Il a également souligné que cette responsabilité ne relève pas de la seule Cellule Genre, mais de l’ensemble des directions, services techniques, projets et programmes du département. « Intégrer l’équité de genre et l’autonomisation des femmes dans l’agriculture et l’élevage, c’est avant tout reconnaître à sa juste valeur la contribution inestimable des femmes et des groupes vulnérables à la souveraineté alimentaire de notre pays », a-t-il déclaré. Le ministre s’est engagé à donner une suite concrète aux recommandations de l’atelier, notamment dans les arbitrages budgétaires, la formation, la sensibilisation et les études sectorielles. Des femmes au cœur de la production, mais loin des ressources Les femmes occupent une place centrale dans la production, la transformation et la valorisation des produits agricoles, ainsi que dans la sécurité alimentaire des ménages. Elles restent pourtant confrontées à des difficultés d’accès au foncier, au financement, aux équipements et aux opportunités économiques. Pour répondre à ces inégalités, le MASAE a mis en place plusieurs instruments depuis 2016. Il s’agit notamment de la circulaire n° 0989 du 5 juin 2018 sur la promotion du genre dans les activités agricoles, des audits genre, des outils de planification et des plans d’action genre dans les domaines du foncier, du riz, de l’énergie productive et du climat. Le ministère a également développé le Programme d’autonomisation économique des femmes dans les secteurs de l’agriculture et de l’élevage (PAEFA). Un Plan d’institutionnalisation du genre (PIG) est par ailleurs en préparation pour le volet élevage. Ces initiatives s’inscrivent dans le cadre de l’Agenda national de transformation Sénégal 2050, de la Stratégie nationale pour l’équité et l’égalité de genre (SNEEG) et de la Loi d’orientation agro-sylvo-pastorale et halieutique (LOASPH). Les services départementaux formés dans les 14 régions Partenaire de la Cellule Genre, le PAIS accompagne la mise en œuvre de son plan d’action à travers des protocoles annuels signés à la suite de l’audit genre du ministère. Son coordonnateur, M. Fall, a cité parmi les principales réalisations l’élaboration du PAEFA et la formation des services départementaux du développement rural (SDDR) des 14 régions du pays sur l’intégration du genre dans le secteur agricole. Il a également salué le partenariat avec l’Agence italienne pour la coopération au développement (AICS), qui ne se limite pas au financement, mais repose également sur une collaboration technique. L’atelier avait pour objectif d’identifier les expériences réussies, les conditions de leur réussite et les moyens de les étendre. Il s’agit d’en faire des outils d’aide à la décision afin de rendre les interventions dans l’agriculture et l’élevage plus inclusives et plus performantes.

items.title: Nouvelle direction de l’OGP : Mohamed Bangoura annonce la couleur et place le redressement au cœur de son mandat
items.description: Installé ce mardi 20 octobre 2026 à la tête de l’Office guinéen de publicité (OGP), Mohamed Bangoura affiche trois priorités : remobliser le personnel, restaurer la confiance des partenaires et améliorer les performances financières de l’institution. Un programme qui s’inscrit dans une volonté de redressement et de modernisation. La cérémonie de passation de service s’est déroulée au siège de l’OGP, à Taouyah, sous la présidence du président du conseil d’administration (PCA), également conseiller personnel du chef de l’État. Elle a réuni le secrétaire général et la cheffe de cabinet du ministère de la Communication, de l’Économie numérique et de l’Innovation, des patrons de presse, d’anciens collaborateurs du nouveau directeur général venus de la Primature, ainsi que l’ensemble du personnel de l’Office. Dans son discours de prise de fonction, Mohamed Bangoura a affiché son ambition de donner un nouvel élan à une institution confrontée à des défis de gestion et de gouvernance. Pour y parvenir, il a résumé sa feuille de route en trois objectifs : « Rassembler nos équipes, rassurer nos partenaires, augmenter nos recettes. » Fédérer le personnel autour d’objectifs communs Pour le nouveau directeur général, le redressement de l’OGP passe d’abord par la mobilisation de ses ressources humaines. Il entend instaurer un environnement professionnel fondé sur le dialogue, la valorisation des compétences et la prise en compte des préoccupations des travailleurs. « Nos différences […] ne doivent pas nous éloigner de notre responsabilité commune : celle de faire progresser l’OGP », a-t-il souligné. Cette volonté de rassemblement ne signifie toutefois pas un relâchement des exigences professionnelles. Mohamed Bangoura a également insisté sur la discipline, la ponctualité, le respect des procédures et le sens des responsabilités. L’objectif est de dépasser les divisions internes pour renforcer la cohésion des équipes et améliorer l’efficacité des services. Restaurer la confiance des partenaires L’amélioration de l’image de l’OGP constitue le deuxième axe de cette nouvelle orientation. Conscient des critiques susceptibles de viser l’institution, le directeur général entend privilégier l’écoute, le dialogue et la concertation avec les acteurs de la publicité et de la communication. « Nous ne pourrons pas empêcher les critiques. Lorsqu’elles sont fondées, nous devons savoir les entendre et corriger ce qui doit l’être », a-t-il reconnu. Il prévoit ainsi de renforcer les échanges avec les opérateurs du secteur, afin de mieux cerner leurs préoccupations, de clarifier les relations professionnelles et de bâtir un climat de confiance durable. Dans un contexte marqué par les perspectives de développement liées au programme Simandou 2040, Mohamed Bangoura estime que l’OGP doit se positionner comme un partenaire crédible, professionnel et prévisible. Une ambition qui repose, selon lui, sur la qualité des services rendus, la transparence des pratiques et la capacité de l’institution à produire des résultats tangibles. Mobiliser davantage de recettes et maîtriser les dépenses Le troisième chantier concerne les performances financières de l’Office. Le nouveau directeur général a rappelé que la disponibilité des ressources conditionne la capacité de l’institution à assurer son fonctionnement, à honorer ses engagements et à répondre aux attentes sociales de ses travailleurs. « Comment faire face à une forte demande sociale si les caisses sont vides ? », s’est-il interrogé, en évoquant notamment la situation de plus de 140 travailleurs sous contrat à durée indéterminée (CDI). Pour inverser la tendance, il préconise une mobilisation plus rigoureuse des recettes, une meilleure organisation des services, l’innovation dans les méthodes de travail et l’exploration de nouvelles perspectives de croissance, dans le strict respect de la réglementation. Cette orientation s’inscrit dans la continuité de certains chantiers engagés sous l’intérim d’Alya Camara, qui a dirigé l’Office durant trois mois avant sa nomination au poste de directeur général adjoint. Celui-ci a fait état d’une progression des recettes et d’efforts visant à maîtriser les dépenses. Il a également évoqué plusieurs initiatives, notamment la digitalisation de certains services publicitaires, le renforcement de l’audit interne et la modernisation du fonctionnement de l’institution. Alya Camara s’est engagé à accompagner son successeur afin de faciliter la transition et d’assurer la continuité des actions entreprises. La tutelle attend des résultats mesurables Prenant la parole au nom du ministère de tutelle, le secrétaire général, Souleymane Thianguel Bah, a rappelé que la nouvelle équipe prend les commandes dans un contexte marqué par des difficultés de gestion et de gouvernance. Il a invité les responsables à tirer les enseignements de cette période pour engager durablement l’OGP sur la voie du redressement. « Le ministère attend de vos équipes des résultats concrets, mesurables et durables », a-t-il déclaré, en mettant l’accent sur la régularité de la gestion, la mobilisation des recettes, la maîtrise des charges et la modernisation de l’établissement. Tout en assurant les nouveaux dirigeants de l’accompagnement du département, il a insisté sur les impératifs de transparence, de responsabilité et de performance. Il a également prévenu qu’il suivrait attentivement leur travail, indépendamment des relations personnelles qu’il pourrait entretenir avec eux. Au-delà des engagements formulés lors de cette passation de service, le véritable défi pour Mohamed Bangoura sera désormais de traduire ses priorités en résultats concrets. La cohésion du personnel, le rétablissement de la confiance des partenaires et l’amélioration des performances financières constitueront autant d’indicateurs pour mesurer l’efficacité de sa nouvelle équipe. L’ambition affichée est de faire de l’OGP une institution plus performante, capable de répondre aux attentes de ses travailleurs, de ses partenaires et du secteur publicitaire guinéen.

items.title: 2027: PDP, APGA, Accord join Tinubu’s re-election campaign — Yilwatda
items.description: -Says ruling party ready for Saturday’s campaign flag-off in Kaduna -As Yari promises issue-based campaign, says APC will showcase Tinubu’s achievements without insults By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA — The National Chairman of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Professor Nentawe Yilwatda, has claimed that major opposition parties, including the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA) and the Accord Party, have aligned with the ruling party’s campaign for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s re-election in 2027. Yilwatda stated this while speaking to State House correspondents shortly after meeting with President Tinubu alongside the Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council (PCC), Senator Abdulaziz Yari, to brief him on preparations for the campaign. He said the development demonstrated the growing political support for the President, adding that the APC had completed preparations for the formal launch of its nationwide presidential campaign in Kaduna on Saturday, October 24. The APC Chairman said the party has attracted support from political parties that previously defeated the APC in elections, a development he described as evidence of the broadening political alignment around the President. According to him: “If you look at what the party is doing now, the oppositions are with us. All political parties that have defeated us in any election are all with us; PDP is with us, APGA is with us, Accord Party with us. These are the only political parties that have defeated us, except APM, and they are all with us in this campaign. “It shows that the entire Nigerian political cycle is Mr. President, and that’s what we’re doing now to ensure that we prepare for this grand flag off in Kaduna”, he declared. He, however, did not specify whether the claimed support represented formal endorsements by the national leaderships of the opposition parties or political alliances involving individual members and groups within them. Yilwatda expressed satisfaction with the level of preparations for the Kaduna campaign launch, saying the party’s leadership, campaign committees and state structures were fully mobilised for the exercise. He explained that his meeting with the President, alongside Yari, was intended to provide an update on arrangements for the event and the readiness of the campaign organisation to commence activities across the country. “We’ll flag-off the campaign on Saturday, 24th of October, and as you can see, we’re together with the DG to brief Mr. President on the preparation for the flag off. “For now, everything is set; the preparation is on, the members are motivated, the states, the committees are ready, and everything that is supposed to be done has been done”, he said. Speaking separately, the Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Abdulaziz Yari, said the ruling party would conduct a responsible and issue-based campaign anchored on the achievements of the Tinubu administration rather than personal attacks against opposition candidates. Yari, a former governor of Zamfara State, said the campaign council had resolved to focus on the record of the APC-led Federal Government and present its accomplishments to Nigerians as the basis for seeking another mandate in the 2027 presidential election. He maintained that the ruling party would avoid insults and name-calling, insisting that its campaign would be driven by evidence of government performance and the argument for continuity. “As a Council, what we say we are going to do? We are going to do a campaign with the records. A responsible campaign, no insults, no calling of names because there’s no name before us, but we have a record before us to show to Nigerians”, Yari stated. He explained that the campaign would provide an opportunity for the party to engage Nigerians on the policies and programmes implemented under the Tinubu administration and make the case for their continuation. “This is what our party did, this what our government did, so because of that, we are asking, pleading Nigerians to look at this record carefully so that they give us a second chance for continuity”, he added. The remarks came as the APC intensified preparations for its nationwide presidential campaign ahead of the 2027 general elections, with Kaduna designated as the venue for the formal flag-off. Yari had earlier announced, following a meeting with Tinubu on October 9, that the President had approved the campaign timetable, including planned visits to states across the federation. The Presidential Campaign Council was subsequently inaugurated on October 14, setting the stage for the commencement of the ruling party’s nationwide mobilisation activities. President Tinubu chairs the campaign council, with Vice President Kashim Shettima and Yilwatda serving as vice chairmen, while Yari oversees the day-to-day coordination of campaign activities as Director-General. The post 2027: PDP, APGA, Accord join Tinubu’s re-election campaign — Yilwatda appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: CRIEF : relaxé pour détournement, mais condamné pour blanchiment, l’ex Inspecteur du Trésor conteste le jugement
items.description: La chambre des appels de la Cour de répression des infractions économiques et financières (CRIEF) a examiné, ce mardi 20 octobre 2026, le dossier d’Almamy Condé, ancien inspecteur des services financiers et comptables à la Direction générale du Trésor public. Alors que la défense conteste plusieurs dispositions du jugement rendu en première instance, le ministère public et l’Agent judiciaire de l’État s’opposent à sa relaxe pour détournement de deniers publics. Le 16 juillet dernier, Almamy Condé avait été relaxé du chef de détournement de deniers publics, mais déclaré coupable de corruption d’agents publics, d’enrichissement illicite et de blanchiment de capitaux. Il avait été condamné à trois ans d’emprisonnement avec sursis, à une amende de deux milliards de francs guinéens ainsi qu’à la confiscation de l’essentiel de ses biens. La chambre de jugement l’avait également condamné à verser dix milliards de francs guinéens à l’État à titre de dommages et intérêts. Cette décision a fait l’objet de plusieurs recours. Me Mamadou Sanoussy Barry, représentant l’Agent judiciaire de l’État, a interjeté appel le 7 août 2026. Le ministère public a ensuite formé un appel incident le 17 août, avant que les avocats de la défense ne contestent, à leur tour, une partie du jugement. Après la lecture du rapport oral, la Cour a donné la parole aux différentes parties pour exposer leurs arguments. Au nom du collectif des avocats d’Almamy Condé, Me Séréba Mory Kanté a indiqué que la défense avait fait le choix de contester partiellement la décision rendue en première instance. L’avocat a notamment remis en question les condamnations pour corruption d’agents publics, enrichissement illicite et blanchiment de capitaux, alors que son client a été relaxé du chef de détournement de deniers publics. « S’il n’a pas détourné de deniers publics, comment a-t-il fait pour blanchir des capitaux ? D’où viennent ces capitaux ? », s’est-il interrogé. Me Séréba Mory Kanté a également demandé à la Cour de préciser l’identité de l’agent public qui aurait été corrompu ainsi que les faits précis imputés à son client au titre de cette infraction. La défense conteste également la condamnation d’Almamy Condé au paiement de dix milliards de francs guinéens à l’État à titre de dommages et intérêts. Selon elle, le préjudice invoqué par la partie civile n’aurait pas été suffisamment établi pour justifier un tel montant. À l’opposé, le ministère public et l’Agent judiciaire de l’État estiment que la relaxe pour détournement de deniers publics ne se justifie pas au regard des éléments du dossier. Ils demandent ainsi à la Cour de revenir sur cette partie du jugement et de retenir la responsabilité de l’ancien inspecteur pour les faits concernés. L’examen en appel porte donc à la fois sur les infractions retenues contre Almamy Condé, la portée de sa relaxe partielle et les sanctions financières prononcées à son encontre.

items.title: NPA, UMaT explore partnership to strengthen Ghana’s downstream petroleum sector
items.description: The National Petroleum Authority (NPA) is exploring a partnership with the University of Mines and Technology (UMaT) to strengthen innovation, technical training and professional development in Ghana’s downstream petroleum industry. The Chief Executive Officer of the NPA, Godwin Kudzo Tameklo, Esq., disclosed this when a delegation from UMaT, led by the Dean of the School of Petroleum Studies, Professor Richard Amorin, paid a courtesy call on him on Tuesday, October 20, 2026. Mr Tameklo said collaboration between the Authority and academic institutions would help advance the industry by promoting research and innovative approaches to addressing challenges in the downstream petroleum sector. “We would want to continue the engagement with academia because we strongly believe that it will propel the downstream industry, because what academia does is to come up with innovative ways of doing things,” he said. He added that the NPA would explore opportunities to offer internships to UMaT students, particularly in the Authority’s technical departments, to expose them to practical industry operations. “The Authority will also be looking at the possibility of offering some students of the University internship opportunities in some of the technical departments of the NPA, because sometimes it is good for the students to have first-hand opportunity to experience things for themselves,” Mr Tameklo said. The discussions also covered special training and secondment opportunities for UMaT teaching staff, the possible inclusion of the university in training programmes under the proposed NPA Centre of Excellence, and the potential retooling of a laboratory at UMaT as part of the initiative. Professor Amorin thanked the NPA leadership for its willingness to collaborate with the university, expressing hope that the discussions would lead to a formal partnership. “We want to say thank you for having us and for having the openness to collaborate with us. We will relay this information to the Vice Chancellor, and hopefully we can firm up some of the discussions we have had going forward,” he said. Both institutions expressed optimism that the engagement would help bridge the gap between academic research and industry practice while supporting skills development and innovation in Ghana’s downstream petroleum industry. The NPA says it remains committed to building partnerships with academic institutions as part of its mandate to regulate, oversee and monitor the downstream petroleum sector.

items.title: Saint-Louis : la DER/FJ prévoit 72,5 millions de FCFA pour 725 bénéficiaires
items.description: En tournée à Saint-Louis, mardi 20 octobre, le délégué général de la Délégation générale à l’entrepreneuriat rapide des femmes et des jeunes (DER/FJ), Dr Abdoulaye Niane, a annoncé un objectif d’enrôlement de 29 groupements, représentant 725 bénéficiaires, pour un montant global de 72,5 millions de FCFA. La pêche, l’agriculture et les industries culturelles figurent parmi les secteurs prioritaires de cette intervention. La DER/FJ veut renforcer son accompagnement des femmes et des jeunes entrepreneurs de Saint-Louis. Lors de cette étape de sa tournée, Dr Abdoulaye Niane a réaffirmé l’ambition de sa structure de soutenir les initiatives économiques locales et de faciliter l’accès aux financements. Pour cette opération, 29 groupements, soit 725 bénéficiaires, sont ciblés pour une enveloppe de 72,5 millions de FCFA. « Ce qui constitue certainement un jalon. Mais ce n’est pas à l’aune de ce que nous comptons faire puisque nous voulons aller très loin, beaucoup plus loin », a déclaré le délégué général. Au-delà du financement des activités naissantes, la DER/FJ entend intervenir dans des secteurs clés de l’économie locale. La pêche occupe une place importante, notamment la transformation des produits halieutiques et la commercialisation du poisson. Dr Abdoulaye Niane a également annoncé des discussions avec les compagnies pétrolières opérant au large de Saint-Louis, en vue de mobiliser des financements en faveur des populations affectées par l’exploitation pétrolière et gazière. « Nous avons bon espoir que dans les semaines à venir, dans les mois à venir, vous verrez des fonds décidés à accompagner les populations », a-t-il indiqué. L’agriculture, notamment la riziculture et l’horticulture, ainsi que les industries culturelles et artistiques, figurent également parmi les domaines d’intervention envisagés. L’adjoint au préfet, Abdou Khadre Dieylani Ba, a salué cette initiative de proximité visant à mieux faire connaître les dispositifs d’accompagnement aux populations. « Il est essentiel que les bénéficiaires potentiels soient suffisamment informés des mécanismes existants, des conditions d’accès aux financements et des obligations qui en découlent », a-t-il souligné. Il a invité les porteurs de projets à privilégier des initiatives « réalistes, viables et créatrices de valeur », réaffirmant la disponibilité de l’administration territoriale à soutenir l’entrepreneuriat local et l’autonomisation économique des femmes et des jeunes. Jeanne SAGNA (Correspondante)

items.title: APC campaign: Tinubu has nothing to say to Nigerians — Baba-Ahmed
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye The National Chairman of the Peoples Redemption Party (PRP), Hakeem Baba-Ahmed, has described President Bola Tinubu as a failure, alleging that the president has nothing to say to Nigerians as the 2027 general election approaches. Baba-Ahmed made the remarks during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Tuesday, while criticising Tinubu’s administration over worsening insecurity, economic hardship and the impact of its policies on Nigerians. “Tinubu inherited Nigeria, but what has he done with it? He inherited a poor country; he inherited weak institutions; he inherited poverty and insecurity. We don’t blame him, but he’s been in power for three and a half years. He is a failure,” he said. The PRP chairman also questioned the president’s reported decision to campaign in only a few places, asking why Tinubu would not commit himself to meeting Nigerians and explaining his policies and the impact on their lives. “Why doesn’t Tinubu commit himself to say, I will. I have the energy, I have the intention, I want to see Nigerians, I want Nigerians to see me, I want them to hear me explain why they are more hungry,” Baba-Ahmed said. Asked why he believed Tinubu had indicated he would visit only a few places during the campaign, Baba-Ahmed replied: “Yes, he has nothing to say to them, I’m telling you, he has nothing to say to Nigerians.” He added: “The reason why he said, Go, gentlemen, go and campaign for me. I will stay here in Abuja and run the country. You’re running the country now? For three and a half years, you didn’t run the country, now you remember that you are here to run the country?” Baba-Ahmed also faulted the administration’s economic reforms, arguing that the difficult decisions taken by Tinubu had hurt ordinary Nigerians rather than improved their lives. “He (Tinubu) made some tough decisions but they were anti-people decisions, a tough decision doesn’t have to be a good decision,” he said. He questioned the impact of the administration’s policies on education, particularly for children living in areas affected by insecurity. “You talk about creating loans, that’s good, but do you know how many millions of children that can’t go to school under Tinubu’s watch in this country? Children who live in territories taken over by bandits, kidnappers, and who can’t go to school at all?” The PRP chairman further alleged that insecurity had deteriorated under the current administration. “Security has gotten considerably worse, it has never been worse like this,” he said. On the administration’s defence of its economic reforms, Baba-Ahmed dismissed the presentation of economic statistics as propaganda, arguing that the figures did not reflect the hardship experienced by ordinary Nigerians. “All these things you mentioned, this is the propaganda. Unfortunately, for Tinubu, Nigerians are not going to buy it. Children are not going to school, life is more insecure, life is harder,” he said. He argued that the president’s appeal for another four-year term would require Nigerians to accept that the current difficulties would eventually give way to better conditions. “He flashes all these statistics, he is saying, give me a second chance, even Tinubu will not say he made lives more better, what he will say is that yes, we are going through a difficult part, if you give me another four years, we will get better,” Baba-Ahmed said. He also questioned the administration’s economic sequencing, arguing that a government anticipating significant economic consequences from its policies should have considered their effects before implementing them. “You said the microeconomics is good, those are statistics that they use and they will tell you, if you give me another four years, I will see them. Sir, if you knew you had four years within which you’ll embark on a profoundly influential policy, shouldn’t you look at it first of all and say, I’m going to have four years and if I embark on these policies, it will have major economic impacts.” Baba-Ahmed added that a president should consider the immediate effects of economic policies on citizens before proceeding with them. “A thinking president will say let me do one or two things first, because I will impoverish people and the cost of transportation is vital and central to everything.” The post APC campaign: Tinubu has nothing to say to Nigerians — Baba-Ahmed appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: From a year at home to Pharmacy distinction: Thompson Kombat’s journey
items.description: Thompson Kawoktu Kombat spent a year at home after completing the West African Senior School Certificate Examination (WASSCE) in 2018 because his family could not afford his university admission fees. Eight years later, he graduated with a Distinction in Doctor of Pharmacy from the University for Development Studies (UDS), with three academic honours to his name, after receiving financial support from the MTN Ghana Foundation’s Bright Scholarship. Thompson gained admission to UDS in 2019, but financing his education remained a challenge. A businessman lent his family money to cover his initial university costs, while he relied on his mobile phone for academic work because he could not afford a laptop. The challenges deepened in his second year when he lost his mother. His father was also struggling to access his retirement benefits. “I lost my mother in my second year, a painful experience that deeply affected me. Around the same time, my father faced difficulties accessing his retirement benefits, which had been locked up in the bank,” he recounted. Determined to complete his education, Thompson searched online for financial assistance and discovered the MTN Ghana Bright Scholarship. He applied, attended an interview and was selected at the end of his Level 300 year. The scholarship covered his tuition and accommodation, provided a stipend for daily expenses and supplied a laptop to support his studies. “For the first time, I felt relief from the constant burden of worrying about tuition and accommodation fees. Before the scholarship, every academic year came with anxiety about how to settle school bills, and that uncertainty often affected my concentration,” he said. He said the support gave him renewed confidence and strengthened his determination to excel. “I recognised that not every deserving or needy student had the opportunity to receive such support. This made me view the opportunity not simply as financial assistance, but as a vote of confidence in my abilities,” he said. Thompson graduated in November 2025 with a Distinction in Doctor of Pharmacy. At UDS’s 26th Congregation, he was named Overall Best Male Graduating Student of the School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences and Overall Best Student in the Department of Pharmacognosy and Herbal Medicine. He has since passed his professional licensure examination and is a registered pharmacist awaiting his housemanship posting. Looking ahead, Thompson hopes to specialise in industrial pharmacy, focusing on drug formulation, development and research. He also plans to pursue a Master’s degree in Pharmaceutical Technology and contribute to Ghana’s pharmaceutical industry. Reflecting on his journey, he said: “Excellence attracts support, and when one is committed and performs well, opportunities will arise through the goodwill of others. That belief inspired me to remain focused and determined throughout my studies.” He expressed gratitude to the MTN Ghana Foundation for helping him complete his education. “This scholarship has made a lasting difference in my life, and for that, I remain sincerely thankful,” he said. Thompson’s story is among the beneficiary experiences being highlighted as MTN Ghana marks 30 years of operations under the theme “30 Years of Progress, Power to You”. The MTN Bright Scholarship supports brilliant but financially disadvantaged students in public tertiary institutions, providing assistance for tuition, accommodation, reading materials and a laptop.

items.title: UK reaffirms commitment to deepen defence, security partnership with Nigeria
items.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The United Kingdom has reaffirmed its commitment to strengthening its longstanding defence and security partnership with Nigeria, with renewed focus on military cooperation, professional military education, institutional capacity building and enhanced operational effectiveness. Director of Defence Information, Major General Samaila Uba said the commitment was reiterated when the recently appointed British High Commissioner to Nigeria, Mr. Pete Vowles, paid a courtesy visit to the Chief of Defence Staff (CDS), General OO Oluyede, at the Defence Headquarters, Abuja. The British High Commissioner expressed appreciation for the enduring political, diplomatic and military relations between both countries, emphasising that defence and security cooperation remain critical pillars of the UK-Nigeria bilateral relationship. He underscored his determination to sustain the momentum of existing security initiatives and explore opportunities to deepen collaboration in response to evolving regional and global security challenges. He further highlighted the importance of maintaining a strong and mutually beneficial partnership that support regional stability and strengthens Nigeria’s capacity to address contemporary security threats. In his response, the CDS highlighted the longstanding historical ties between Nigeria and the United Kingdom, noting that both countries have sustained a productive defence relationship for several decades and continued to work together in addressing shared security concerns. General Oluyede emphasised the importance of sustaining and expanding existing areas of cooperation, particularly in professional military education, transfer of technology and institutional capacity building. He noted that ongoing defence agreements and training programmes have contributed to enhancing the professional competence and operational capabilities of the Armed Forces of Nigeria. The CDS stressed that continued collaboration with strategic international partners remains important to strengthening the Armed Forces’ capacity to respond effectively to emerging threats, while promoting greater self-reliance, institutional resilience and operational efficiency. Both parties expressed optimism about the future of the UK-Nigeria defence and security partnership, reaffirming their commitment to building on existing achievements and identifying further areas of cooperation for mutual benefit. items.title: Ogun Assembly backs establishment of state police
items.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The Ogun State House of Assembly has thrown its weight behind the proposed establishment of state police, passing a resolution in support of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026. The resolution, titled “H.R. No. 194/OG/2025 – Consideration of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria (1999) (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026 (Establishment of State Police Services),” was passed during plenary, following the consideration of a report by the House Ad-hoc Committee on Constitutional Review. The committee, chaired by a former Speaker of the Assembly, Rt. Hon. Olakunle Oluomo, presented its report on 26 clauses and proposed amendments to various sections of the 1999 Constitution. Presenting the report, Oluomo took the proposed amendments one after another, with lawmakers voting in favour of all the clauses and sections contained in the proposals. The amendments covered various aspects of the bill, including the substitution, insertion and alteration of specific constitutional provisions aimed at providing a legal framework for the establishment of state police services. Following the consideration of the proposed amendments, Oluomo moved a motion for the adoption of the committee’s report. The motion was seconded by Hon. Adegoke Adeyanju and subsequently supported by the lawmakers through a voice vote. The House Leader, Hon. Yusuf Sherif, thereafter moved a motion for the adoption of the report as a resolution of the Assembly. The motion was seconded by the Chief Whip, Hon. Omolola Bakare, and unanimously supported by members through a voice vote. Speaking after the passage of the resolution, the Speaker of the Assembly, Rt. Hon. Oludaisi Elemide, said the Assembly had joined other state legislatures across the country in supporting the establishment of state police, describing the decision as historic. Elemide said the resolution reflected the position of the lawmakers and the people of Ogun State on the need to strengthen the country’s security architecture through the establishment of state police services. According to him, the initiative would help improve security measures and enhance the protection of lives and property, while promoting the social well-being and economic development of the state. He added that the proposed establishment of state police was an important step towards addressing security challenges and strengthening the capacity to safeguard communities. Following the passage of the resolution, the Speaker directed that a clean copy of the document be prepared and transmitted to the National Assembly to formally communicate Ogun State’s support for the proposed constitutional amendment. The resolution forms part of the ongoing constitutional amendment process through which state legislatures are considering proposed changes to the 1999 Constitution, including the proposal to establish state police services.
